## TL;DR - From October 10 to November 15, 2026 - 52 kilometers between Locarno and Domodossola - Just under two hours each way - Ticket valid for one or two days ## Key facts - Event → Treno del Foliage - Railway → Ferrovia Vigezzina-Centovalli - Route → Locarno-Domodossola - Distance → 52 kilometers - Duration → just under two hours per leg - Validity → one or two days - Stop → an intermediate stop on the outbound or return journey From October 10 to November 15, 2026, the Treno del Foliage returns to the Ferrovia Vigezzina-Centovalli. The journey connects Locarno and Domodossola, passing through wooded areas and gorges, over bridges and alongside villages, in an Alpine setting lit up by autumn colors. For a Frontaliere Ticino reader, the central point is the railway connection between Ticino and Piedmont. The route crosses the Centovalli and Valle Vigezzo, along a historic line that connects the two areas. The route covers 52 kilometers and takes just under two hours per leg. ### A recognized itinerary The Ferrovia Vigezzina-Centovalli offers one of the most evocative panoramic itineraries in the Alps. Lonely Planet and the New York Times have included it among the ten most beautiful railway routes in the world. The autumn landscape is therefore the focus of the experience described, alongside the connection between the two locations. Launched in 2016, the Treno del Foliage has become an autumn classic and over the years has attracted an audience from beyond the local area. For the 2026 edition as well, the ticket may be valid for one or two days. You can depart from Locarno or Domodossola; the ticket also allows an intermediate stop along the route, to be made on the outbound or return journey. Claudio Blotti, director of FART, considers the initiative one of the symbols of the Ferrovia Vigezzina-Centovalli. In his statement, he describes the journey as something that goes beyond transportation and brings together landscape, slowness, territory, and discovery. The stated aim is to promote the railway during the Foliage and throughout the year, with new experiences on board and at destinations along the line. For guidance on connections from Ticino, the internal reference to mezzi pubblici Ticino accompanies the itinerary information. ## How to read the offer for those crossing the border For a cross-border commuter travelling between Ticino and Piedmont, the flexibility indicated in the source lies mainly in the choice of endpoint and ticket validity. A single departure point is not specified: Locarno or Domodossola can be chosen. This choice allows the journey to be planned from whichever side of the border is more convenient for the reader, without changing the line described. ### Four choices to keep separate The structure of the offer can be read as follows: | Element | Available option | |---|---| | Endpoint | Locarno or Domodossola | | Validity | one or two days | | Intermediate stop | possible along the route | | Stop timing | on the outbound or return journey | This distinction serves to avoid confusing the departure with the stop. The former can be chosen from the two endpoints of the line; the latter can be added along the route, with the choice of placing it on the outbound or return journey. For those who want to plan their day without committing to a single direction of travel, this is the most tangible feature of the 2026 ticket. Validity for one or two days offers two distinct formats. With one day, the journey centers on the experience provided for by the ticket; with two days, validity extends across two days. The difference does not change the line, the endpoints or the possibility of stopping: it changes the time available to organize the route. The route also has geographical value for the Frontaliere Ticino audience. The line connects Ticino and Piedmont via the Centovalli and the Vigezzo Valley, covering 52 kilometers and offering autumn scenery along the journey. For this audience, its usefulness therefore lies in the cross-border rail connection associated with a seasonal experience. To place the two ends of the route in the context of the border, one can consult mappa valichi, keeping the geographical orientation separate from the ticket options for the Treno del Foliage. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## From choice to the day The simplest way to organize the outing is to start with the elements described for the 2026 edition. The journey is defined by the period, the two termini, the validity of the ticket, and the possibility of making an intermediate stop. ### The five steps 1. Choose a date between 10 October and 15 November 2026. 2. Select the starting point between Locarno and Domodossola. 3. Decide whether to use a ticket valid for one or two days. 4. Consider whether to include an intermediate stop on the outbound journey or on the return journey. 5. Use 52 kilometres and a duration of just under two hours per journey as a reference. This sequence applies both to those departing from the Ticino side and to those departing from Piedmont. The start of the journey changes, not the nature of the route: the historic line crosses the Centovalli and Valle Vigezzo, alternating wooded areas, gorges, bridges and villages, while the Alpine landscapes take on autumn colours. For a cross-border commuter, the most relevant choice is deciding how to use the connection between Ticino and Piedmont. The source allows you to set the journey from either end, choose a validity of one or two days, and place the stop along one of the two directions. These are the practical decisions that define the experience. The perspective outlined by Claudio Blotti goes beyond a single edition: FART's objective is to promote the railway both during the Foliage period and throughout the rest of the year, by developing new experiences on board and at destinations along the line. item.title: Trade unions petition for cost-of-living compensation in Ticino
item.description: ## TL;DR - OCST, VPOD and SIT are calling for compensation for inflation. - Between December 2020 and September 2026, inflation increased by approximately
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - OCST, VPOD and SIT call for recovery of the cost-of-living adjustment. - Between December 2020 and September 2026, the cost of living increased by approximately 8,5%. - Salaries were adjusted by only 3%. - For 2027, the Government expects 0,25%. ## Key facts - Promoters → OCST, VPOD and SIT - Recipients → State Council and Grand Council - Period considered → December 2020-September 2026 - Cost-of-living increase / salary adjustments → approximately 8.5% / 3% - Adjustment planned for 2027 → 0.25% Between December 2020 and September 2026, the cost of living increased by approximately 8.5%, while salaries received adjustments amounting to only 3%. Based on these figures, OCST, VPOD and SIT are launching a petition addressed to the State Council and the Grand Council. The request consists of two points: making up for the failure to recognize the cost-of-living increases of previous years for public, parapublic and social-healthcare personnel, and ensuring full recovery of the cost-of-living increase from 2027 onward. As part of the debate on the 2027 Budget, the unions reiterate their opposition to the cuts and their impact on working conditions and public services. For a cross-border worker who works in Canton Ticino, the connection is concrete but conditional: it concerns those who hold a position in the sectors indicated and whose pay is tied to the Canton’s salary scale. The text links the mobilization to personnel and sectors covered by the scale, not to a separate measure for those who live across the border. ### The sectors indicated by the unions At the center is the failure to fully recognize the cost-of-living increase for cantonal staff. According to the unions, the repercussions extend to sectors whose pay is tied to the Canton’s salary scale: EOC, nursing homes, public SACD, USI, SUPSI, OSI and numerous municipalities. This list gives the cross-border worker an initial way to interpret the issue: employment at EOC, USI, SUPSI or in one of the other areas mentioned may make the mobilization relevant. However, the petition remains a request addressed to cantonal decision-makers and does not describe an individual change that has already been secured. For an initial comparison of one’s pay, simulatore busta paga is available. For 2027, the Government is planning an adjustment of 0.25%, which the unions consider too limited to make up for the losses accumulated in recent years and to offset the current rise in the cost of living. According to their estimate, on a monthly salary of 5'000 francs, the loss amounts to approximately 3'500 francs per year. > According to the unions, defending real wages is not a privilege but a matter of fairness and respect for those who provide essential services to the population every day. ## The difference still matters after the first year The petition is not limited to the adjustment planned for 2027. OCST, VPOD and SIT describe a loss of purchasing power that accumulated because, between December 2020 and September 2026, the cost of living rose faster than wages. For a cross-border worker, the practical question is whether the job held falls within a sector whose pay is linked to the Canton's salary scale. The figure of approximately 3'500 francs per year should be understood in the same way. It is the estimate for a monthly salary of 5'000 francs; it is not an amount assigned indiscriminately to every employee. The petition calls for recovery of the unrecognized cost-of-living adjustment, but does not describe a payment that has already been arranged. This distinction avoids confusing a union claim with an automatic credit on the payslip. ### The long-term effects indicated | Element analyzed | Indicated effect | |---|---| | Immediate effect | Loss of purchasing power | | Effect on raises | Lower salaries affect subsequent raises | | Social security effect | Lower salaries affect social security contributions | The unions' reasoning goes beyond the current month: a lower wage base can affect subsequent raises and social security contributions. For those working at EOC, in nursing homes, in public SACDs, at USI, at SUPSI, at OSI, or in a municipality included on the list, the comparison therefore also concerns wage progression. An identical loss for everyone cannot be inferred from belonging to the category alone. The costs cited by the unions — health insurance, petrol, energy and rents — explain why defending real wages is presented as an issue of fairness. A cross-border worker can consider the costo della vita Ticino vs Italia alongside the data, keeping the personal comparison and the general estimate contained in the petition separate. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the petition To turn the news into concrete action, a cross-border worker employed in Canton Ticino can start with the steps outlined in the mobilization. The process involves checking the sector, supporting the initiative and taking part in the events announced by the unions. ### Four practical steps 1. Identify the sector. Compare your field with EOC, nursing homes, public SACD and numerous municipalities. The source also mentions USI, SUPSI and OSI. The criterion indicated is the link between remuneration and the Canton’s salary scale. 2. Read the full request. The petition aims, for public, parapublic and social-healthcare staff, to make up for the cost-of-living increase left uncompensated in previous years and to ensure full compensation for inflation from 2027. When assessing your own position, it is important to distinguish between these two objectives. 3. Sign or support it. OCST, VPOD and SIT are addressing the staff concerned and the public, inviting them to sign the initiative or support it. The invitation therefore concerns both workers in the sectors indicated and anyone wishing to back the request. 4. Mark November. The petition is scheduled to be submitted at the November session of the Grand Council and will be accompanied by a protest action in the square. The source identifies that session as the public moment for the submission and mobilization. When making the comparison, use the example of 5'000 francs per month with caution: the estimate of approximately 3'500 francs per year refers to that salary level and does not replace an individual assessment. For those crossing the border, the useful reference remains their own position in a sector linked to the cantonal scale. The mobilization calls for support for the defense of real wages, while the unions point to the costs of health insurance, petrol, energy and rent. To obtain an indicative assessment of your remuneration, use calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [ticinonews.ch](https://www.ticinonews.ch/ticino/carovita-i-sindacati-lanciano-una-petizione-per-il-recupero-dei-salari-444061)*

item.title: Domodossola: arrest for a kilo of hashish in luggage
item.description: ## TL;DR - Stopped at the international station of Domodossola - Was arriving from Milano Centrale - One kilogram of hashish in ten bricks - Estimated value
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Stopped at the international station of Domodossola - Was arriving from Milano Centrale - One kilogram of hashish in ten bricks - Estimated value: over 10mila euro at retail
## Key facts - Location → Domodossola international station - Origin → Milano Centrale - Substance → hashish - Quantity → one kilogram - Packages → ten blocks - Estimated value → over 10mila euros at retail - Authority → Domodossola Guardia di finanza - Outcome → arrest and transfer to Vercelli
A Guardia di finanza check at Domodossola international station led to the arrest of a woman arriving from Milano Centrale. When officers asked her whether she had any goods or currency to declare, the passenger replied, “nothing to declare.”
Her nervousness nevertheless aroused the officers’ suspicions. They therefore decided to inspect the luggage more thoroughly, going beyond the initial answer given during the check.
### From luggage to seizure
Inside the paper bag, they found ten blocks: tests identified them as hashish, with a total weight of one kilogram. According to estimates, a potential retail sale could have yielded over 10mila euros.
The operation was carried out by officers from the Domodossola Company of the Guardia di finanza, who were engaged in customs surveillance and economic control of the area at the international station. The activity is aimed in particular at combating illicit trafficking and the smuggling of narcotics.
The officers informed the public prosecutor on duty at the Public Prosecutor’s Office in Verbania of the discovery.
The check forms part of inspections conducted by the Guardia di finanza along the border and at international transit points, aimed at intercepting drug trafficking and other forms of illegality having a greater impact on public safety and public health.
As provided by law, the woman must be considered innocent until any conviction becomes final. ## The meaning of the check for those passing through
For those using an international transit point, the sequence described shows a concrete fact: the initial declaration did not conclude the check. The financial police officers asked about the presence of goods or currency to declare; after the passenger's response and the nervousness they noticed, they decided to inspect the luggage more thoroughly. The source describes the intervention as customs surveillance and economic control of the territory, not as a communication about work or taxation.
### The figure does not equal seized cash
The economic figure should be read within its exact scope. Over 10mila euro is the estimate of what the hashish could have fetched if it had been put on the retail market. The source does not present that sum as money found or as an amount seized. The material fact indicated, instead, is one kilogram of the substance, divided into ten bricks; the seizure concerns the drug.
The judicial stage also has a precise meaning. After the discovery, the Public Prosecutor's Office of Verbania was informed through the prosecutor on duty. The woman was arrested and taken to the Vercelli prison, but the text keeps the charge distinct from the final outcome of the proceedings: the presumption of innocence applies until any final, unappealable judgment.
### What the source does not indicate
The report does not indicate delays, closures, cancellations or diversions in transport connections, nor does it describe consequences for passenger traffic. It also does not attribute similar checks to every traveler. For this reason, the link with those crossing the border remains limited to a documented fact: the operation took place at an international station and falls within checks along the border and at international transit points.
The picture, therefore, is operational and judicial: luggage inspection, identification of the substance, seizure, notification to the Public Prosecutor's Office and arrest. The source makes it possible to reconstruct a precise sequence of the operation, but does not add any steps beyond those indicated. Set out in operational form, the procedure reported is as follows.
### The five steps reported in the source
1. Arrival at the station. The woman reaches the international station of Domodossola, arriving from Milano Centrale. 2. The officers’ question. The Guardia di finanza asks whether there are any goods or currency to declare. The passenger replies that she has nothing to declare. 3. More thorough inspection. Her nervousness arouses the suspicions of the officers, who decide to check the luggage. 4. Discovery and investigation. Ten packets are found in a paper bag; investigations identify them as hashish, with a total weight of one kilogram. 5. Judicial follow-up. The public prosecutor on duty at the Public Prosecutor’s Office of Verbania is informed; the substance is seized and the woman arrested, then taken to Vercelli prison.
The sequence separates the different stages of the operation: customs surveillance carried out at the station, inspection of the luggage, identification of the substance and referral to the judicial authorities. The text links the activities of the Domodossola Guardia di finanza Company to a broader system of economic control of the territory, along the border and at international transit points.
The charge concerns Article 73, paragraph 4, of Dpr 309/90, which governs the unlawful production, trafficking and possession of narcotic substances. This is an accusation, not a conviction: the person under investigation remains innocent until a possible final, unappealable judgment. The source does not indicate any further deadlines or decisions by the judicial authorities.

item.title: Como-Switzerland trains: 4 weekends of closures in 2026
item.description: ## TL;DR - Four closure weekends between October and November 2026 - Stop from Friday at 20:20 to Monday at 04:20 - RE80 skips Como San Giovanni and Como
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Four closure weekends between October and November 2026 - Service suspended from Friday at 20:20 to Monday at 04:20 - RE80 skips Como San Giovanni and Como Camerlata - There is a connection with S11 trains at Cucciago ## Key facts - Works → scheduled maintenance by RFI - Tunnel → Monte Olimpino 1 - Diversion → Monte Olimpino 2 - S10 and S40 → to and from Chiasso - Check → online, FFS Mobile or Contact Center FFS Cross-border rail traffic between Como and Switzerland will be subject to changes on four weekends between October and November 2026. The Monte Olimpino 1 tunnel will be affected by maintenance work planned by Rete Ferroviaria Italiana (RFI) and will therefore remain closed during the scheduled periods. The closure will begin at 20:20 on Friday and end at 04:20 on Monday morning. For cross-border commuters, the time window is the first thing to check: the closure covers the specified weekend, from Friday evening until the early hours of Monday. The change affects the TILO RE80, TILO S10, TILO S40 and EuroCity services, but not in the same way. The overview therefore distinguishes between the tunnel used, stops and route limits. ### RE80, S10, S40 and EuroCity TILO RE80 trains bound for or coming from Milano Centrale will use the Monte Olimpino 2 tunnel. Consequently, during the closure, the trains will not stop at Como San Giovanni or Como Camerlata. An exceptional stop will be introduced at Cucciago, allowing passengers to reach or leave the Como stations by connecting to Trenord S11 trains. For the RE80 service, this is the solution planned during the closure. TILO S10 and TILO S40, on the other hand, will have their routes shortened. They will run only to and from Chiasso. EuroCity trains to and from Milano Centrale will also be diverted via Monte Olimpino 2 and will not stop at Como San Giovanni. These instructions apply both to services heading towards Milano Centrale and to those in the opposite direction. To navigate skipped stops, diversions and limitations, passengers are advised to check the timetable for the individual train before setting out. The indicated tools are online consultation, the FFS Mobile app and the Contact Center FFS. For rail commuting, you can find out more about mezzi pubblici Ticino. For a cross-border commuter, the notice should be read as a set of instructions linked to the service chosen, not as the same change for everyone. The route between Como and Switzerland can change in three ways: diversion with stops skipped, service limited to Chiasso, or diversion with the Como San Giovanni stop excluded. This distinction helps interpret your journey without assigning the same change to RE80, S10, S40 and EuroCity. ### The comparison between services | Service | During the closure | Point to check | |---|---|---| | TILO RE80 | Via Monte Olimpino 2 | Como San Giovanni and Como Camerlata skipped; connection at Cucciago with S11 | | TILO S10 and S40 | Route limited to and from Chiasso | Route limitation | | EuroCity | Diverted via Monte Olimpino 2 | No stop at Como San Giovanni | The first comparison to make is between the scheduled service and the station concerned. If the journey involves RE80 and boarding or alighting was scheduled at Como San Giovanni or Como Camerlata, those stops are not available during the window. Cucciago is the exceptional stop indicated for making the connection with Trenord's S11 towards the stations in Como or in the opposite direction. For S10 and S40, the restriction applies in both directions: the train runs to Chiasso or departs from Chiasso. For EuroCity, the change concerns the tunnel and the Como San Giovanni stop: the connection to and from Milano Centrale is diverted via Monte Olimpino 2. The boundary of the time window also matters. A departure after 20:20 on Friday falls within the closure, as does a journey scheduled before 04:20 on Monday morning. The same time period is indicated for the four weekends. For this reason, the calendar alone is not enough: it must be matched with the selected service. For a separate assessment of the costs of commuting by car, you can consult costo auto pendolare, without using it as a substitute for checking the train. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. When one of the four weekends approaches, the commuter's procedure starts with the individual service and continues with checking whether assistance is available. The source indicates precise tools and deadlines. ### Procedure before departure 1. Check the timetable of the individual train online before setting off. The check must concern the service actually selected, not just the general connection. 2. Use the FFS Mobile app as a second consultation channel. This allows you to check the timetable of the service indicated for the journey before departure. 3. If you prefer telephone contact, call the Contact Center FFS. From a Swiss landline, the number is 0848 44 66 88, at a cost of 0,08 CHF/min. 4. If you need assistance boarding or alighting from trains in Swiss territory, book it at least one hour before departure. From Switzerland, the toll-free number 0800 007 102 is available; from abroad, you can call +41 800 007 102. The service is active from 5:00 to 24:00. 5. If the support request concerns Italian territory, submit it at least 48 hours in advance to 800 210 955. The number is active every day from 8:15 to 19:45. The two assistance requests therefore have different deadlines: one hour in advance in Swiss territory and 48 hours in advance in Italian territory. The numbers also vary depending on where support is needed. Otherwise, the timetable check remains available online, on the FFS Mobile app or via the Contact Center FFS. item.title: Fake banker scam in Luino: 17 thousand euros seized
item.description: A 32-year-old man from Campania has been reported: he allegedly convinced a 62-year-old person to make a bank transfer. An account containing more than 17,000 euros was seized.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - A 32-year-old man from Campania was reported - A 62-year-old victim was contacted on their mobile phone - A false alarm led to a bank transfer - An account containing more than 17,000 euros was seized ## Key facts - Location → Luino Carabinieri Station - Charge → fraud - Method → fake digital payments operator - Measure → preventive seizure of the bank account - Amount → more than 17,000 euros A 32-year-old man from Campania was reported by the Carabinieri at the Luino Station after a rapid investigation and is currently considered responsible for fraud against a 62-year-old Luino resident. The victim was contacted on their mobile phone by a stranger. The man presented himself as an operator for a private company specializing in digital payment services. During the call, he made the danger of potential fraudulent withdrawals from the victim's bank account seem real. That false emergency led the person contacted to make a large bank transfer to the suspect. The sequence described by the officers centers on the shift from reporting a banking risk to asking that money be transferred to the account linked to the 32-year-old. The victim then went to the Luino Carabinieri Station to report what had happened. That report led to subsequent checks on the account identified as the recipient of the bank transfer. ### From the call to the initial response The sequence described in the investigation comprises a few steps: the phone contact, the false professional identity, the warning about withdrawals, and the bank transfer. No withdrawal made directly by the caller is described; the conduct at issue concerns inducing the victim to transfer the money for his benefit. The report was filed after the bank transfer, when the 62-year-old reached the station in Luino. The 32-year-old is identified as a suspect and is currently considered responsible. The report therefore concerns the fraud allegation reconstructed by the officers, while the checks followed the trail of the account identified as the recipient of the bank transfer. ## The dynamics of fake emergencies The method described by the Carabinieri is based on a fake telephone emergency. The caller presents himself as having an identity connected to a digital payments service and introduces the issue of possible fraudulent withdrawals. In the case handled in Luino, the warning was the story presented by the stranger to obtain a bank transfer. The source reports, in fact, that the man pretended to be an employee of a private company specializing in digital payment services. The reminder from the officers concerns not only the case that has already taken place. The Carabinieri renew their appeal to all citizens to pay the utmost attention to fake telephone emergencies. The warning includes requests for money and jewelry: people must not trust anyone who, for any reason, asks for them over the phone. The same caution applies to personal data, which must not be provided to strangers. ### Guidance for citizens The officers' message also extends attention to attempted scams. The request is to contact law enforcement immediately, without waiting for the phone call to turn into actual harm. In the case of Luino, the speed with which the victim reached the Station is identified as the factor that made it possible to act quickly on the account. This is the link between the report and the subsequent investigation: a timely report enabled the Carabinieri to carry out the banking checks. The recommendations remain practical. A phone call must not become a reason to hand over money or jewelry, or to communicate personal data to a stranger. The fact that the caller invokes a company specializing in digital payments does not change the Carabinieri's invitation to remain extremely vigilant when faced with a telephone request. The recommendation is addressed both to those who have already responded to a suspicious request and to those facing an attempt that is still ongoing. The source emphasizes that contacting law enforcement is also recommended when the scam is merely attempted, not only when the bank transfer has already been made. ## The current account identified by the military In the phase following the report, immediate banking checks enabled the carabinieri to identify the bank where the current account held in the suspect's name was maintained. The outcome of the checks led to the preventive seizure of the account and the freezing of the balance mentioned in the investigation. The account had a balance of over 17 thousand euros. The funds were duly frozen and remain pending their return to the victim. The situation described is therefore that of a blocked amount, while the return is indicated as the next step. ### The next step indicated in the source The matter does not end with the account being identified alone. The report paved the way for the checks, the seizure preserved the balance, and the return to the victim is indicated as the expected step. The information communicated by the carabinieri is that the over 17 thousand euros are frozen pending return. For the public, the operational follow-up indicated is to contact law enforcement. In case of the slightest suspicion, the carabinieri invite people to contact the Single Emergency Number 112 or the Stations present in the area with confidence. The same indication applies when the scam is only attempted, because the source emphasizes the importance of an immediate report. The outcome communicated is therefore twofold: on the one hand, the report by the 32-year-old from Campania, and on the other, the preventive seizure of the account with the balance frozen. Any return is still described as forthcoming, not as an operation already completed. *Source: [varesenoi.it](https://www.varesenoi.it/2026/10/06/leggi-notizia/argomenti/cronaca-20/articolo/deruba-unanziana-con-la-truffa-del-finto-operatore-bancario-i-carabinieri-di-luino-gli-sequestrano.html)*

item.title: Ticino Parliament: A2-A13 to become a USTRA priority again
item.description: Ticino Parliament votes on a resolution not to postpone the A2-A13 connection beyond 2050. Locarnese is the only major region without direct motorway access.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Ticino Parliament supports the resolution on A2-A13. - No votes against; seven abstentions from the Greens and MPS. - The proposed postponement would go beyond 2050, perhaps to 2055. - The Government considers the Trasporti '45 programme insufficient. ## Key facts - Body → Ticino Parliament - Subject → A2-A13 motorway link - Request → return to USTRA's priority projects - Vote → no votes against and seven abstentions - Region → Locarnese - Time frame → beyond 2050, perhaps not before 2055 - Federal programme → Trasporti '45 - Government position → step in the right direction, but insufficient On Tuesday, the Ticino Parliament supported, almost unanimously, a resolution addressed to the Federal Council. The request is precise: the A2-A13 motorway link must not be postponed further and must return to USTRA's priority projects, USTRA being the Federal Roads Office. In a hypothetical scenario, a cross-border commuter whose destination is in the Locarnese would be faced with a planning decision concerning direct access to the motorway. The resolution, however, does not describe a new opening: it records the political request concerning the future of the link. calcolatore fiscale remains outside this account: the issue here is infrastructure priority, not the individual's situation. The vote met with no opposition. There were no votes against, while the seven abstentions came from the Greens and MPS. It was recalled in the chamber that the Locarnese remains the only major Swiss region without direct motorway access. This is the territorial factor that supported the request not to postpone the project again. ### The position of the Ticino Government The concern expressed in the chamber stems from the Confederation's plan to postpone construction of the link beyond 2050, perhaps not before 2055. Speaking on behalf of the Government, State Councillor Raffaele De Rosa said: «This is a postponement that cannot be proposed». In recent days, the Ticino Government had stated its position on the Confederation's Trasporti '45 programme. The assessment given was that it was a step in the right direction, but insufficient to meet the Canton’s needs. The same statement expressed concern about the postponement of the Bellinzona-Locarno link. The resolution thus brings the issue to the federal level. The Ticino Parliament is asking the Federal Council not to postpone A2-A13 any further and to return it to USTRA's priorities. The source links this request to the Locarnese's lack of direct access and the Government's opposition to a postponement beyond the stated horizon. ## The issue for those traveling through the Locarnese For cross-border commuters, the news conveys a practical distinction: the debate concerns the planning of a connection, not an immediate change to the route. For anyone who, in a hypothetical scenario, has the Locarnese as their destination, the discernible point is the uncertainty of the timeframe, not a new timetable, a new construction site or an alternative road indicated by the source. The useful comparison is between the objective expressed by Parliament and the scenario challenged in the chamber. On the one hand, A2-A13 should avoid further delays and return to USTRA's priority projects. On the other, construction has been placed in a timeframe beyond 2050, perhaps no earlier than 2055. The two perspectives do not produce the same timeframe for a region that Parliament defines as Switzerland's only large region without direct access to the motorway. ### Politics is not yet a timetable The resolution is not equivalent to the construction of the project. It is a request addressed to the Federal Council and, at the same time, a political signal about the project's place among USTRA's priorities. For this reason, no opening date can be inferred from the vote: the available text does not indicate one. Nor is the Trasporti '45 program presented by the Ticino Government as a sufficient response to the Canton’s needs; the assessment is more nuanced, because the program is considered a step in the right direction but insufficient. The reference to Bellinzona-Locarno adds the cantonal dimension to the discussion. The Ticino Government had expressed concern precisely about the postponement of that connection, while Parliament focused its resolution on A2-A13. For the cross-border commuter reader, this means distinguishing between the project’s name, the venue of the request and its possible future construction. A cross-border commuter in a similar situation could use a simple sequence, based solely on the steps reported: identify the project, distinguish the political request from its implementation, and verify the timeframe mentioned in the chamber. 1. **Identify the project.** The main reference is the A2-A13 connection; the Ticino Government's position also refers to the Bellinzona-Locarno connection. The two references should be kept as presented by the source, without adding technical details. 2. Read the request. The Ticino Parliament asks the Federal Council not to postpone the connection any further and to put it back among USTRA's priority projects. 3. Distinguish between what is hypothetical and what is certain. Beyond 2050, perhaps not before 2055, is the timeframe indicated by the Confederation as a hypothesis and challenged in the chamber; it is not a definite opening date. 4. Track the institutional follow-up. The point to verify in any updates is whether the request from Ticino is taken up at the federal level and whether the project is once again among USTRA's priorities. ### What not to add to the news story The text does not provide timetables, travel times, alternative routes, costs, construction sites or documents to submit. item.title: Part-time work pays less percentage-wise
item.description: In Ticino, 65% of employees work full-time (5'456 francs/month) and 35% part-time with an equivalent remuneration of 5'121 francs, that is, 335 francs less.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In Ticino, 65% of salaried workers work full-time. - Part-time work concerns 35% of salaried workers. - For the same working hours, the average gap is 6,1%. - In Switzerland, part-time work concerns 38,5% of salaried workers. ## Key facts - Source→new October report by Ustat - Data→2024 - Full-time in Ticino→65% and 5'456 francs per month - Part-time in Ticino→35% and 5'121 francs in full-time equivalent - Ticino gap→335 francs less - Comparison for the same working hours→6,1% less for part-time work - Switzerland→38,5% part-time and 7,7% gap - Motion→Evaristo Roncelli calls for an analysis by the State Council The 6,1% is the average difference that emerges, for the same working hours, between the salary of those who work part-time and that of those who work full-time. The figure is contained in the new October report by the Statistical Office (Ustat), but the analysis invites us not to stop at the percentage: when comparing only workers with similar characteristics, the differences tend to disappear. ### The 2024 picture In 2024, in the Canton of Ticino, 65% of salaried people worked full-time and earned an average of 5'456 francs per month. The remaining 35% worked part-time; their full-time-equivalent remuneration was 5'121 francs, or 335 francs less. Ustat describes a stable situation: in 2014, the difference between the two groups was very similar. ### Women, age and profile The report indicates that it is predominantly women who work part-time, often in sectors offering lower remuneration. Age also matters: part-time work is more common among the youngest and oldest age groups. The picture changes when the comparison is made between workers with similar characteristics. In that case, the differences between full-time and part-time work tend to disappear: what affects remuneration is the employee's profile, not the percentage worked. ### The comparison and the motion In the Swiss comparison, part-time work is more common, at 38,5%, and the wage gap reaches 7,7%. The trend, however, is different: since 2014, the increase in part-time wages has been more pronounced than that of full-time wages. Ustat hypothesizes that over the past decade, people with high remuneration chose part-time work, raising the average. Yesterday, in the Grand Council, the motion by Evaristo Roncelli, of Avanti con Ticino&Lavoro, was approved, calling on the State Council to analyze disposable income as work percentages vary. The motion's proponents fear that higher income and the loss of certain subsidies may leave the same amount at the end of the month. ## The percentage is not enough The aggregate figure is useful for describing the market, but it is not enough to judge the attractiveness of an individual job. A lower average for part-time work brings together people who, according to Ustat, differ in age, gender and sectoral placement. If the comparison is narrowed to workers with similar characteristics, the gap tends to shrink until it disappears. The correct question, therefore, is not only what percentage one works, but which profile is being compared. ### For those who work across the border For a cross-border worker working in the Canton of Ticino, this caution avoids an excessive reading of the figure. The available text contains no distinctions between residents and non-residents, nor a calculation referring to the G permit. The source focuses on salary and offers no information on AVS, LPP or LAMal. Nor does it address withholding tax and double taxation. These aspects, therefore, cannot be inferred from the comparison between full-time and part-time work. The passage on disposable income raises a different issue. The motion approved by the Grand Council stems from the concern that a person already employed part-time may not be incentivized to increase their working percentage: the increase in income could be accompanied by the loss of entitlement to certain subsidies, leaving the amount available at the end of the month unchanged. It is not a new salary measure described by the source, but a request for an analysis that considers working percentages, income and subsidies together. To turn the comparison into a personal assessment, readers can place the simulatore busta paga alongside Ustat's data. If the question concerns the money left at the end of the month, costo della vita Ticino vs Italia offers a second perspective, without attributing to these statistics a precision that the source does not provide. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## An operational reading The source does not establish what percentage is appropriate for each worker and does not offer an individual procedure. To use the data without attributing answers to it that it does not contain, the reader can follow four steps. 1. Start with the reference year. Use 2024 to read the snapshot of the Ticino labor market and 2014 to verify the time comparison indicated by Ustat. 2. Keep the two salary dimensions distinct. On the one hand, there is full-time work; on the other, for part-time work, full-time-equivalent remuneration. The difference of 335 francs should be read within this statistical framework. 3. Check the profile being compared. Women, age groups and sectors do not have the same weight in the composition of the groups. The report invites readers to compare workers with similar characteristics before attributing the difference solely to the percentage worked. 4. Separate salary from disposable income. The scenario concerning subsidies is why the motion calls for a specific analysis as the percentage of work varies. It should not be confused with the salary comparison prepared by Ustat. For a cross-border worker who works in Ticino, this sequence makes it possible to use the statistics as a reference without turning them into an answer about individual conditions that the source does not examine. The institutional step to follow is the analysis requested from the State Council; the available text does not anticipate any results. item.description: Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 14:30 to 16:30, the Salone Estense in Varese hosts the presentation of the WHP Program of Regione Lombardia, organized by ATS Insubria, Municipality, Confindustria and ASST Sette Laghi.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The WHP program will be presented in Varese on October 7, 2026 - Event at Salone Estense from 14:30 to 16:30 - ATS Insubria collaborates with the Municipality, Confindustria and ASST - Focus on well-being, prevention and sustainability at work ## Key facts - What → Presentation of the WHP Program of Regione Lombardia - When → Wednesday, October 7, 2026, from 14:30 to 16:30 - Where → Salone Estense in Varese - Organizers → ATS Insubria, Comune di Varese, Confindustria Varese and ASST Sette Laghi ### The event in Varese On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, Salone Estense in Varese will host the public meeting dedicated to the presentation of the WHP Program, an acronym for Workplace Health Promotion, of Regione Lombardia. The event is scheduled from 14:30 to 16:30 and will be organized by ATS Insubria in collaboration with Comune di Varese, Confindustria Varese and ASST Sette Laghi. The stated objective is to promote a culture of well-being, prevention and sustainability within companies and organizations in the area. The initiative is dedicated to good practices in corporate welfare and prevention in workplace settings and aims to provide an opportunity for discussion among institutions, businesses and professionals. The WHP Program will be presented through the practical tools made available to companies to counter behavioral risk factors and promote healthy lifestyles. These materials will be complemented by firsthand accounts from several local organizations that have already joined the network. The names mentioned include Eurojersey, Fondazione Comi Onlus and Comune di Varese itself. The Municipality therefore appears both among the parties collaborating on the organization and among the organizations invited to share their experience within the WHP network. The announced format brings together the institutional level, dialogue with the business community and the contribution of professionals, maintaining the focus on welfare and prevention practices in the workplace. The collaboration between ATS Insubria, Comune di Varese, Confindustria Varese and ASST Sette Laghi has accompanied the event from its organization onward. item.title: Como and Lecco: risk of losing 14 thousand workers by 2029
item.description: UIL warning: lack of housing, complex commuting and inadequate services risk driving thousands of working-age people away from the area.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - By 2029, Como and Lecco risk losing over 14 thousand working-age people - In the Como area, 54,5% of the profiles sought are impossible to find - ASST Lariana: 40 hires out of 170 nursing positions - The Tremezzina bypass is scheduled for 2031 - Who → UIL Lario, UILFP Lario Brianza and UIL Scuola Como - Area → provinces of Como and Lecco - Horizon → by 2029 - Work → 54,5% of the profiles sought in the Como area are impossible to find - Healthcare → 170 nursing positions, 40 hires; 45 positions for family and community nurses, 10 recruited By 2029, the provinces of Como and Lecco risk losing over 14 thousand working-age people. The warning was issued by UIL Lario, UILFP Lario Brianza and UIL Scuola Como, which put the attractiveness of the area at the center of the debate. A solid economy and strong demand for labor, according to the organizations, are no longer enough to persuade people to live and stay in the area. In the Como area, the signal is already measurable: 54,5% of the profiles sought by businesses are impossible to find due to a lack of candidates. ### The paradox of essential services UIL identifies the strengthening of public services as a precondition for economic development. To make Como attractive, healthcare, schools and efficient public administrations are needed. Yet the same sectors struggle to attract and retain staff. Healthcare makes the problem concrete. In the competition announced by ASST Lariana for 170 permanent nursing positions, only 40 people were hired because the ranking list was exhausted. For the 45 positions for family and community nurses, only 10 people were recruited. > «We cannot seek nurses, teachers and public-sector staff without asking ourselves where they will be able to live and how they will be able to get around» They explain it in unison: Dario Esposito, coordinator of UIL Lombardia Lario, Massimo Coppia, general secretary of UILFP Lario e Brianza, and Gerardo Salvo, general secretary of UIL Scuola Como. The sentence sums up the point of the complaint: a job offer cannot be separated from the material conditions of the area. For a cross-border commuter reading these data, the reference to the Milan-Como-Chiasso line is one of the explicit links to daily mobility: the source mentions over 26 thousand daily travelers. It does not add schedules, individual travel times or alternative routes. To stick to the documented figure and explore only the topic of connections, the mezzi pubblici del Canton Ticino are available. ### Housing, mobility and schools are not separate chapters A practical reading of the UIL complaint starts with a change of perspective. Having a job available is not enough if a person cannot find housing, manage daily travel or integrate their family into local services. This is also relevant to the cross-border commuter who views the Como area as a place to live, without turning the source into a guide to cross-border rules. The first filter is housing. Rising prices and the growth of the so-called «grey area» make finding housing an insurmountable obstacle. The source uses this term for those who cannot access public housing but cannot afford the costs of the free market. | Issue | Evidence reported | What it indicates | | Housing | Rising prices and growth of the «grey area» | Finding housing can become an insurmountable obstacle | | Mobility | More than 26 thousand travelers on the Milan-Como-Chiasso line; Como-Lecco is single-track and diesel-powered; the Tremezzina bypass is scheduled for 2031 | Complex connections weigh on daily life | | Schools and services | Educational provision and the network of personal services | An indispensable condition for the stable integration of families | The most useful point for the cross-border commuter is the coexistence of these three issues. The number of travelers shows the scale of mobility on the Milan-Como-Chiasso line, but the source does not indicate how many are cross-border commuters and does not distinguish between the different reasons for travel. The reference to the Como-Lecco line and the Tremezzina bypass likewise describes infrastructure and expected timelines, not an individual solution. To avoid misunderstandings, the scope does not include the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax revenue shares, withholding tax or double taxation: the source provides no data on these areas. Its contribution concerns a territory’s ability to retain people through housing, mobility, schools, healthcare and public administration. To supplement this reading with a housing check, you can consult costo della vita in Ticino e in Italia. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ### A four-step check The source does not propose forms, offices, or documents to submit. The possible action is therefore an assessment framework built around the issues identified by UIL, without turning territorial data into an administrative procedure. 1. Set the timeframe. Note the two time references found in the source: by 2029 for the risk of losing working-age people and 2031 for the expected completion of the Tremezzina bypass. They are not personal deadlines, but dates useful for understanding the evolution of the area. 2. Assess housing. Describe the necessary housing solution and check whether rising prices or belonging to the «gray area» represent an obstacle. The source does not provide rents, addresses, or financial thresholds: values not contained in the text must not be added. 3. Reconstruct mobility. Consider the Milan-Como-Chiasso line, the Como-Lecco connection, which is still single-track and uses diesel traction, and the Tremezzina bypass. The source points to complex connections, but does not indicate schedules, individual travel times, or alternative routes; the assessment must remain anchored to these elements. 4. Focus on schools and services. If the choice involves a family, include in the assessment the school provision and the network of personal services, identified as essential conditions for stable integration. If it concerns healthcare, school, or public administration, supplement the application with the question of where to live and how to get around. For a cross-border worker, this checklist separates the documented territorial conditions from the information the source does not provide. After collecting these items, compare disposable income with calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/senza-case-mobilita-e-scuole-le-province-di-como-e-lecco-rischiano-laddio-di-14mila-persone/)*

item.description: The Giubiasco FFS station building will reopen on 8 October 2026 after work costing approximately 6,4 million: new services, lift and Minergie standards.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Reopening to the public: 8 October 2026 - Investment: approximately 6,4 million francs - New lift and Minergie standard - Three commercial businesses on the ground floor - Location → Giubiasco FFS station - Reopening → 8 October 2026 - Investment → approximately 6,4 million francs - Duration → several years - Accessibility → new lift - Heating → heat pump - Energy standards → Minergie - Ground floor → three commercial businesses On 8 October 2026, the Giubiasco FFS station building will reopen to the public. The date marks the end of a redevelopment project that lasted several years, with a total investment of approximately 6,4 million francs. FFS has completed the full renovation of the passenger building, one of the most important railway hubs in the Bellinzona area. ### A renovation involving structure and energy The work did not focus on just one element of the building. The project addressed the structural, energy and functional aspects together, with the aim of adapting the building to the current needs of users, commercial businesses and services. For anyone passing through the station, this means finding a building redesigned in its main components, without separating access, technology and the internal offering. The construction work included renovating the façades and roof, completely renewing the technical and electrical systems, replacing doors and windows and installing a new lift. item.title: Carvivita, the unions demand recovery of the gap in the 2027 Quote
item.description: Between December 2020 and September 2026, the cost of living rose by 8.5%, while the salaries of cantonal, parapublic and social-healthcare staff were adjusted by only 3%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Unions demand cost of living adjustment in the 2027 Budget - Between December 2020 and September 2026, inflation rose by 8.5% - Affected salaries were adjusted by 3% - For 2027, the Government recognized 0.25% ## Key facts - Objective → recover cost of living for public, parapublic, and social-healthcare personnel - Promoters → OCST, VPOD, and SIT - Recipients → Council of State and Grand Council - Period → December 2020-September 2026 - Inflation → approximately 8.5% - Salary adjustment → 3% - Example → 5,000 monthly francs and approximately 3,500 francs in annual loss - 2027 Measure → 0.25% cost of living recognized by the Government Between December 2020 and September 2026, inflation increased by approximately 8.5%, while the salaries of affected employees were adjusted by only 3%. This is the data on which the three Ticino unions, OCST, VPOD, and SIT, base their petition addressed to the Council of State and the Grand Council. The request is included in the 2027 Budget: to recognize the cost of living adjustment not granted in recent years and to compensate for the actual inflation of 2027. The initiative arises at a time that the petition describes as difficult for Ticino residents, amidst health insurance, petrol, energy, and rents. To track the impact of these items, you can also consult the cost of living, without attributing data to the tool different from those reported in the source. ### Who is included in the claim The claim directly concerns cantonal personnel. It also includes a large part of the parapublic and social-healthcare sectors, when remuneration is linked to the Canton's salary scale. The text mentions EOC, nursing homes, public SACD, USI and SUPSI, OSI, and numerous Municipalities. The union document quantifies the effect with a case already indicated in the source: someone earning 5,000 francs monthly can suffer a loss of approximately 3,500 francs per year. The petition adds that the discrepancy is not exhausted by the adjustment of a single year. A lower salary remains so throughout a career, impacts subsequent increases, and reduces pension contributions. For 2027, the Government recognized only 0.25% for the cost of living. According to the petition, this measure does not recover previous losses and would not even compensate for current inflation. The source does not directly mention cross-border commuters, but the point is relevant for anyone working in Canton Ticino within one of the indicated categories: the verification concerns the link between one's remuneration and the cantonal salary scale. ## The gap revealed by the payslip For a cross-border commuter working in one of the listed structures, the practical point is not the worker's origin, but the criterion by which remuneration is set. The source, in fact, links the pay to the Canton's salary scale. This narrows the analysis: the petition cannot be automatically extended to anyone working in Ticino, but neither can it ignore those who fall under the indicated cantonal, semi-public, or social-healthcare personnel. ### Three numbers, three different moments | Reference | Data | What it indicates | |---|---:|---| | December 2020-September 2026 | 8.5% | The inflation detected | | Same period | 3% | The adjustment of affected salaries | | Year 2027 | 0.25% | The cost of living recognized by the Government | The comparison shows a recovery that, according to the unions, has not kept pace with the increase in inflation. The example of 5,000 francs per month makes the difference concrete: the indicated annual loss is approximately 3,500 francs. To understand one's own situation, it's not enough to look at a single item from one month; remuneration must be placed within the trajectory described by the petition, keeping separate the adjustment already granted, the arrears recovery, and the compensation foreseen for 2027. The payslip simulator can help organize the already available items, without transforming the result into a figure different from that indicated by the unions. The second effect concerns time. The petition speaks of lower salaries throughout one's career, consequences on subsequent raises, and reduced pension contributions. For a cross-border worker, this part is as important as immediate spending: the problem described is not only the purchasing power in the autumn, but the possible persistence of the gap in future remunerations. The source does not quantify these effects beyond the annual example, thus not allowing for the calculation of a further individual loss. The political fact is equally clear: the request is directed at the 2027 Budget, while the Government has recognized 0.25%. As long as one sticks to the contents of the source, the possible comparison is this: recovery of the gap and compensation for actual inflation, on one hand; the measure recognized for 2027, on the other. The source maintains the comparison on these two levels. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## From News to Personal Verification For a cross-border commuter working in Canton Ticino, the most prudent action is to transform the union's request into a circumscribed check, without confusing it with a measure already applied to every salary. The source provides some fixed points and allows one to proceed without adding unindicated amounts or deadlines. ### Four Verification Steps 1. **Identify the scope.** Check if your position falls within the cantonal staff or the cited parapublic and social-healthcare sectors. The decisive criterion indicated by the petition is the link between remuneration and the Canton's salary scale. Named entities include EOC, USI, and SUPSI, in addition to other structures and municipalities mentioned. 2. Set the comparison period. Read the salary situation relative to the interval between December 2020 and September 2026. The petition compares an 8.5% inflation with a 3% adjustment for the affected salaries. The case of 5,000 francs monthly and an annual loss of about 3,500 francs is the numerical reference provided by the source, not a result to be automatically applied to every worker. 3. Separate the recovery from the 2027 measure. The request concerns both the cost of living not granted in recent years and the compensation for actual inflation in 2027. The Government, however, recognized 0.25% for 2027. Keeping these elements distinct avoids interpreting that figure as a full recovery of previous losses. 4. Follow the indicated recipients. The petition is addressed to the Council of State and the Grand Council and links the request to the 2027 Budget. For those working across the border, the aspect to monitor therefore remains the salary and institutional one described by the source, not an automatic modification of an individual's position. This verification helps to understand if the news truly concerns one's own remuneration and to distinguish general data from the example reported by the unions. To translate the available data into an understanding of your remuneration, use the salary calculator. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/politica/1954970/carovita-i-sindacati-chiedono-al-cantone-di-recuperare-il-divario)*

item.title: Cross-border workers: entry tax, tax rebates and double taxation
item.description: Switzerland is introducing an entry tax of up to 4 thousand francs for employees and self-employed workers. There is discussion of 900 million annually for the unemployed, and there is a risk of 120 million for border municipalities.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Entry tax of up to 4 thousand francs for employees and self-employed workers - Switzerland votes against 900 million annually for cross-border workers - The roundtable on health tax and double taxation was on September 17 - 120 million at risk for border municipalities ## Key facts - Entry tax → up to 4 thousand francs - Allowance for unemployed cross-border workers → 900 million francs - Interministerial roundtable → September 17 - Average salary in Switzerland → 5.500 francs more in one year - Border municipalities → 120 million at risk - Legacy cross-border workers → data transmitted for the first time Up to 4 thousand francs for employees and self-employed workers: this is the item that opens the page on cross-border workers. The opening headline asks who pays it, without adding any further answer in the available material. Alongside this item is Switzerland's no to the 900 million francs per year intended for cross-border workers. ### From health tax to tax rebates The same roundup lists a tax bonus for those who spend in Ticino and, on another level, the interministerial roundtable of September 17 devoted to health tax, double taxation and status. The sequence thus connects workers, taxation and relations between Italy and Switzerland, but leaves the individual headlines distinct. The transfers section concerns border municipalities: the decree on the funds due to the administrations appears to have been signed. The page places alongside this news the item on the allowance for unemployed cross-border workers, described as a sum of 900 million charged to Switzerland, with the clarification that Switzerland can say no. The list also includes the risk of 120 million for municipalities bordering Switzerland. Regarding the health tax, the headlines record a conflict between the Ticino government, the Swiss government, Regione Lombardia, and Italian and Swiss trade unions. One speaks of a possible halt to ristorni; another calls the stoppage a violation of the agreements. After 912 days, the unions are still attacking and maintain that the health tax is a tax, not a contribution. > “The health tax is a tax, not a contribution” The salary-related thread completes the picture. Pre-filled tax returns allegedly revealed protected data about cross-border workers' salaries, with accusations of privacy violations and demands for compensation. Another headline reports 5.500 francs more in one year for the average salary in Switzerland, approaching 100 thousand. Finally, the section on legacy cross-border workers mentions an error in the data, an Irpef alert and the transmission of that data for the first time. For a cross-border worker who works in the Canton of Ticino, the first practical distinction is between the income-tax line and the political debate over tax rebates. Tax on employment income is withheld at source only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in section CE of form 730. This mechanism alone is not equivalent to a decision on the health tax. ### Dates and categories that change the reading The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement was signed on 23 December 2020 and has been in force since 1 January 2024. Therefore, the expression new 2026 tax agreement should not be used to indicate the effective date of that agreement. The distinction between old and new cross-border workers changes the tax-free allowance: | Item | Verified rule | |---|---| | Old cross-border workers | Already in that category before 17 July 2023; €7'500 exemption; transitional regime 2024–2033 | | New cross-border workers | €10'000 tax-free allowance | The Convention on double taxation between Italy and Switzerland dates from 9 March 1976, and Switzerland is not an EU/EEA member. These are reference points that help avoid confusing the tax reference with the rest of the issues that appear in the overview. The cross-border worker must also keep the G permit, AVS, LPP and LAMal separate: they are distinct matters from the calculation of withholding tax, the health tax and tax rebates. The tax aspect must then be checked in dichiarazione dei redditi, while AVS e LPP and LAMal do not replace checking the income tax assessment. This separation prevents every item in the Italy-Switzerland relationship from being read as if it were a deduction from the salary. ### Four checks before doing the math The figure of up to 4mila francs appears in the headline as an entry tax for employees and self-employed workers. It must therefore not automatically be turned into a personal withholding: the headline specifically raises the question of who pays it. The verification must start from the nature of the item, not only from the amount. 1. Start from July 17, 2023. Anyone who was already a cross-border worker before that date belongs to the group of old cross-border workers; the indicated transitional regime covers the period 2024–2033. For new cross-border workers, the verified allowance is €10'000. 2. If the doubt concerns employment income, separate the withholding tax deducted in Switzerland from the tax credit in section CE of the 730. Do not add the two items together as if they were the same tax. 3. If the health tax appears, treat it as a question separate from double taxation and from ristorni. The headlines in the roundup in fact show a discussion about its nature, alternatively described as a tax or contribution, and a conflict over the blocking of transfers. 4. If the check concerns the cross-border-worker headline, use the reference to permesso G/B without confusing it with the tax calculation. If instead you are reading a salary figure, consider the extra 5.500 francs as a figure referring to the average salary in Switzerland, not as an automatic increase in your payslip. This sequence makes it possible to distinguish status, income, healthcare and transfers without attributing to the individual worker figures that the source refers to categories or averages. To turn the salary figure into an estimate of net pay, use calcolatore fiscale. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/argomento/frontalieri/#)*

item.title: Unemployment stable at 3% in Switzerland in September 2026
item.description: In September, unemployment in Switzerland remains at 3% and in Ticino at 2,9%, with 4'800 unemployed, while job vacancies rise to 44'200.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Swiss unemployment at 3% in September. - Ticino at 2,9%, with 4'800 unemployed. - In Switzerland, 140'500 registered with the URCs. - Announced vacancies are 44'200.
## Key facts - National rate → 3% in September. - Ticino → 2,9% in September. - Grisons → 1,1% in September. - ILO comparison → 4,9% in the second quarter. - Registered with the URCs → 140'500.
Swiss unemployment stood at 3% in September, unchanged from August and July. SECO reported that, at the end of the year's ninth month, 140'500 unemployed people were registered with the regional employment offices (URCs): 1'100 fewer than in August and 7'200 more than a year earlier. Absolute figures are rounded to the nearest hundred for ease of reading. Over twelve months, however, the national rate rose by 0,2 percentage points.
In January 2021, at the most critical point of the pandemic, nearly 170'000 people without work had been recorded, with the rate at 3,7%. For those who live near the border and work in the Canton of Ticino, this comparison provides a general measure of the market in which they operate; section disoccupazione frontalieri should, however, be kept separate from SECO's official figure.
### The Ticino figure in the Swiss context
In Ticino, the rate stood at 2,9% in September, unchanged from August and up by 0,3 percentage points year-on-year. From Airolo to Chiasso, there were 4'800 unemployed: 100 more than in the previous month and 400 more than a year earlier. Ticino ranks 11th among the territories most affected by the problem; Geneva and Vaud are experiencing greater difficulties.
The Grisons recorded a rate of 1,1%, unchanged from the previous month and down by 0,1 percentage points year-on-year. In the canton whose capital is Chur, there were 1'200 unemployed, unchanged. The Grisons rank fifth among the least affected territories, led by Appenzell Innerrhoden.
The statistic has a precise scope. It counts people actually registered with the URCs and does not include those who have exhausted their entitlement to benefits and live, for example, on savings or welfare. The definition therefore differs from that of the International Labour Organization (ILO), which is based on surveys: in the latest available figure, referring to the second quarter, Swiss unemployment according to the ILO was 4,9%. ## The differences that matter to those who work across the border
A cross-border worker observing the labor market in Canton Ticino must start from the measured population. People registered with the URC are a different group from people seeking employment: the latter includes, in addition to registered unemployed people, workers attending retraining or further-training courses, participating in employment programs, or earning an interim income. Last month, people seeking employment numbered 227'600, up 0,2% compared with August.
For a cross-border worker, this marks an editorial boundary: the bulletin measures unemployment, not issues such as the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates and withholding tax. These elements should not be inferred from the percentages published by SECO.
### Age, nationality and duration
The age brackets show three distinct figures: 3,3% among young people aged 15 to 24, 3,2% among 25- to 49-year-olds and 2,6% among over-50s. The breakdown by nationality instead indicates 2,1% for Swiss nationals, unchanged month on month and with +0,1 year on year, and 5,1% for foreign nationals, unchanged month on month and with +0,2 year on year.
Another signal concerns the duration of the job search. The long-term unemployed numbered 25'600, 0,1% more than in August and 25,4% more than twelve months earlier; among them were 10'300 people over 50. The figure therefore adds to the monthly snapshot a measure of the length of registration with the URC.
The number of vacancies announced at placement offices was 44'200, with 500 more than in the previous month and 6'800 more than in the previous year. Anyone who wants to pair the statistic with a search for opportunities can consult the annunci lavoro, keeping overall availability and their own situation separate.
Short-time work also has a different reference period: in June, the latest available figure, it concerned 840 people. In September, by contrast, 3'000 people exhausted their entitlement to unemployment insurance benefits.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## A procedure for reading the next update
When SECO releases a new overview, a cross-border worker can use five simple checks. The goal is not to place on the same footing indicators based on different populations or periods.
### Five practical checks
1. **Set the period**: indicate whether the data concern September or June, as in the case of short-time work, for which the most recent information was available. 2. Identify the indicator: distinguish the percentage rate, the number of people registered with the URCs, people seeking employment, and the ILO survey. 3. Note the comparison: record whether the change is monthly or annual, because the source presents both readings. 4. Check the territory: distinguish the Swiss figure from those for Ticino and the Grisons before making comparisons. 5. Complete the form: add, when available, age group, nationality, length of registration, job vacancies, and short-time work.
The first check prevents directly comparing data referring to different months. The second reminds us that the number of people registered with the URCs does not coincide with all people seeking employment, while the ILO figure comes from surveys and has a different definition.
The third step serves to avoid confusing a change relative to August with a change over twelve months. The fourth prevents automatically attributing to the Canton of Ticino a figure referring to Switzerland as a whole. Finally, the form must indicate that absolute figures are rounded to the nearest hundred and that some values, such as job vacancies or short-time work, have a specific time frame.
To turn this reading of the labor market into a personal estimate of your paycheck, use calcolatore stipendio.
