## TL;DR - In 2025 in Ticino: 97 conversions of sentences or fines. - In Zurich, 1'388 requests in the Infopoint's first year. - Four hours of work count as one day of imprisonment. - The success rate of the Zurich model is between 75 and 80%. ## Key facts - What → community service instead of a fine or sentence - Eligible sentences → up to six months in prison - Ratio → 4 hours of work equal 1 day in prison - Minimum commitment → at least 8 hours a week - Requests in Zurich → 1'388 - Success rate → 75-80% - Available companies → almost 250 - Ticino in 2025 → 97 cases ## The situation in Zurich and Ticino In 2025, 97 people in Ticino converted sentences or fines into community service. In previous years, based on the available data, the figure hovered around one hundred. The exception was 2024, with 125 cases. This figure runs counter to what was observed at national level, where a decline had been recorded compared with 2023. ### A voluntary option In Zurich, a foundation was established last year to promote the option offered by the justice system of performing community service instead of paying a fine or serving a sentence. The choice must come from the person concerned: there is no automatic process, and not all sentences allow recourse to this solution. Fines, monetary penalties and sentences of up to six months in prison can be converted. The source cites speeding, driving under the influence and using public transport without a valid ticket, an issue that those travelling in Ticino can explore further in the guide to trasporti pubblici in Ticino. In the event of reoffending, fines can quickly become very high, and the person is not always able to pay them. The alternatives indicated are prison or conversion. The ratio established by the model is precise: four hours of work in a hospital, even washing dishes, correspond to one day of imprisonment served. At least eight hours must be completed each week, while also complying with a series of rules for the sentence to be considered served or the fine paid. The option has existed for some time and was strengthened in 2007 with the entry into force of the new Swiss Criminal Code. After an initial increase and a period of stability, recourse to this solution declined in 2019; in German-speaking Switzerland, the reduction reported was one third. Zurich responded by intensifying promotion and creating the Fondazione Infopoint. In its first year, the new model received 1'388 requests, about 40% more than in the previous period, also thanks to leaflet distribution and plain language. Community service was granted to practically everyone who requested it. ## The practical reading for those who work across the border For a cross-border worker, this news should be kept separate from questions concerning the G permit, AVS, LPP and LAMal. The source does not cover withholding tax, tax revenue transfers or double taxation: its scope is fines, sentences and community service activities. For those who travel for work, the relevant point is limited to the examples cited: the text does not set out special rules for cross-border workers. ### The choice is not an automatic discount Conversion replaces the required service; it does not cancel the sanction. If the sentence is among those eligible, the person may choose to work instead of paying or serving time in prison; access is not automatic. Personal willingness comes first, while the hours and rules of the program determine whether the sentence will count as served. For those who use a car on their commute, speeding and driving under the influence are the road-related examples in the source. costo auto pendolare remains a separate issue, however: here the point is the legal consequence and the possibility of replacing it with an activity, not calculating travel expenses. The same criterion applies to public transport without a valid ticket. ### What the Zurich results show The first year of Fondazione Infopoint offers an operational perspective. The increase in requests was linked to distributing flyers and using easy language; almost all the people who contacted the service were given the opportunity to carry out an activity in the public interest. The success rate, however, remained between 75 and 80%: making a request does not mean that the program succeeds. Almost 250 companies throughout the Canton offer placements. When difficulties arise, counselors support people to prevent the program from being interrupted. The source links this support to the ability to find suitable activities and maintain the process. There is also the cost to the community. The people who carried out the activities did not go to prison; they worked. For the administration, this means less bureaucratic work and savings, because one day in prison costs 240 francs. The Ticino figure remains more stable than the trend observed in German-speaking Switzerland, but the source does not automatically transpose the organizational model described for Zurich to Canton Ticino. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## The operational steps described by the source The procedure can be read as a sequence of checks. The person must want to choose community service: there is no automatic placement. In the account of Zurich, the Infopoint Foundation was created to promote this possibility. ### 2. Verify the type of conviction The second step is to distinguish between the permitted sanctions and the others. The source includes fines, monetary penalties and sentences of up to six months in prison. It also mentions speeding, driving under the influence and using public transport without a valid ticket. Not all types of conviction allow conversion. ### 3. Measure the commitment required The substitution requires a measurable commitment: four hours of activity correspond to one day in prison and at least eight hours must be completed each week. The other program rules must still be followed. Only in this way can the sentence be considered served or the fine paid. ### 4. Identify the activity and manage difficulties In the Zurich model, one can work, for example, in a hospital washing dishes. Almost 250 companies spread throughout the Canton make jobs available. If difficulties arise, counselors support the person to prevent the program from being interrupted; the stated success rate is between 75 and 80%. ### 5. Distinguish the Ticino figure from the Zurich procedure For Ticino, the source records 97 people in 2025, around one hundred in previous years and 125 in 2024. The operational procedure described, however, is that of Zurich: the Ticino figure measures the use of the solution, while the organizational steps concern the Zurich model. The point is not merely to find a job. Success depends on the combination of a suitable activity, weekly attendance and compliance with the rules; the source specifically links the possibility of avoiding interruption to this management. item.description: Carabinieri operation in Albate: 111 grams of cocaine, hashish and 390 euros seized. Two Tunisian citizens arrested, a third reported.

## TL;DR - Saturday, October 3, 2026: two arrests in Lipomo - 111 grams of cocaine seized - Roxy finds hashish and more cocaine - A third Tunisian national reported to authorities ## Key facts - Date → Saturday, October 3, 2026 - Location → municipality of Lipomo, near an apartment building - Operation → Carabinieri of the Albate Station - Support → Casatenovo Canine Unit - Seizure → 111 grams of cocaine, a precision scale and 390 euros ### The Carabinieri operation On Saturday, October 3, 2026, the Carabinieri of the Albate Station arrested two Tunisian nationals and reported one of their compatriots. The charge listed for the group was possession of narcotics with intent to distribute, acting jointly. The operation took place in the municipality of Lipomo, near an apartment building. The investigation involved the personnel of the Como Company working in coordination with support from the Casatenovo Canine Unit. The first part of the checks concerned the suspects and their cars. Searches led to the discovery and seizure of 111 grams of cocaine, a precision scale and 390 euros in cash. The sum was considered proceeds of the illegal activity. The material was found in the possession of two of the people detained, aged 31 and 26, respectively. Both were domiciled in the area between Como and Lipomo, and they were immediately placed under arrest. The sequence described therefore begins with checks on the vehicles and ends with the seizure of the substance, instrument and money. The first operation established the status of the two Tunisian nationals later arrested, while the third compatriot's case was addressed in the subsequent phase. The precision scale and 390 euros were found together with the 111 grams of cocaine during the initial searches. The reconstruction places the extension of the searches to the homes after this initial activity involving the suspects and their cars. ## The discovery in the home ### The role of Roxy The second phase of the operation shifted from the cars to the suspects' homes. It was during this stage that Roxy's keen sense of smell proved decisive. The dog is a drug-sniffing German shepherd working with the Casatenovo canine unit, the same unit that had supported the personnel of the Como Company. Thanks to its keen sense of smell, an additional quantity of drugs was discovered inside the apartment: 28 grams of hashish and approximately one gram of cocaine. The reconstruction therefore distinguishes the material found during the initial checks from that discovered during the search of the home. The apartment belongs to a third Tunisian national, 27 years old and residing in Lipomo. His situation differed from that of the two men arrested in the first phase: the twenty-seven-year-old was already subject to house arrest with an electronic monitoring bracelet. For the latter, the outcome of the intervention was a report without arrest for the same drug-dealing offense. The report links the accusation to the discovery made in the home, while attributing to the two nationals aged 31 and 26 the arrest that followed the seizure carried out from the suspects and their cars. Roxy's presence therefore characterized the home search. The dog enabled the Casatenovo canine unit to locate both the hashish and the second quantity of cocaine mentioned in the reconstruction, expanding the material seized in the operation. ## The outcomes indicated in the report The final outcome of the operation concerns three people and two different outcomes. The two Tunisian nationals, aged 31 and 26, residing between Como and Lipomo, were arrested after searches of the suspects and their cars found 111 grams of cocaine, a precision scale, and 390 euros in cash. According to the source, they were immediately handcuffed. The third case concerns the 27-year-old Tunisian national residing in Lipomo, owner of the home searched in the second phase. The find in the apartment, made with Roxy's assistance, consisted of 28 grams of hashish and about one gram of cocaine. The man was already under house arrest with an electronic ankle bracelet. A report was filed against the 27-year-old, who remained at liberty, for the same offense of drug dealing. The reconstruction therefore separates the outcome of the two arrests from that of the report, while linking the three cases to the accusation of joint possession of a narcotic substance for the purpose of drug dealing. The subsequent development indicated remains that of the intervention just described: two arrests and one report, with the searches moving from the suspects and their cars to the homes. The report adds no other stages, but establishes the role of the Casatenovo Canine Unit in the discovery made in the apartment. The report also distinguishes the locations associated with the different outcomes: for the two arrested men, the searches of the suspects and their cars; for the third, the apartment in Lipomo. The home search is the one in which the contribution of the drug-sniffing dog is mentioned. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/lipomo-il-fiuto-infallibile-di-roxy-scopre-la-droga-due-arresti/)*

item.title: Health insurance funds: 5% increase and proposals evaluated by experts
item.description: In 2027, the premium will increase by 5%. Three experts analyze the state fund, prevention and costs: in Ticino, from 2029, half of citizens could benefit from reductions.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In 2027 the national monthly premium will increase by 5% - Three independent experts assessed the proposals - LAMal administrative costs: around 4% of premiums - Prevention accounts for around 1.5% of healthcare spending ## Key facts - National increase → 5% in 2027 - Social insurance management costs in France → 3% - Healthcare expenditure financed directly in France → 97% - Management costs of private insurance in France → 21% - LAMal administrative costs → around 4% of premiums - Prevention in Switzerland → around 1.5% of healthcare spending - Savings from catalogue checks → around 150 million francs per year - Estimate for Ticino from 2029 → half of citizens with premium reductions In 2027 the national monthly premium will increase by 5%. Last week, the new increase in health insurance premiums for next year was announced. Numerous user proposals were submitted to the dialogue community; three independent experts examined them and commented on some of them. ### State-run fund and management costs A proposal envisions a state-managed health insurance fund, with subsidies for policyholders. The possible advantage indicated by users is a lower premium: without the aim of generating profits or distributing dividends, management could cost less. The comparison brought into the discussion concerns France. In social insurance, management costs are reported at 3%; 97% of healthcare expenditure directly finances medical services. For private insurance, management costs amount to 21%. The proposed conclusion is therefore that the public sector would be much more efficient. Christina Vetsch-Tzogiou, from Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW), shifts the focus, however, from profit to the cost structure. For mandatory health insurance under LAMal, health insurers may not make profits, while administrative costs represent around 4% of premiums. Cost growth depends mainly on the increase in expenditure per person treated, linked to medical progress, the growing use of services and possible overtreatment. In this assessment, a single fund would probably not solve the problem. ### Prevention and organization of care The proposals collected also call for stricter laws in the food sector, from a sugar tax to Nutri-Score, as well as a ban on highly processed products and limits on margins for healthy products. The promotion of sport and early, systematic screening activities for certain diseases are also mentioned. Cécile Grobet, from ZHAW, recalls that Switzerland allocates around 1.5% of healthcare expenditure to health promotion and prevention. In her view, a national strategy, clear objectives and an evaluation of costs and benefits are needed. The effect on premiums in the coming years would not be conclusive, but prevention could contribute in the long term to reducing the number of sick people. Igor Francetic, from SUPSI, considers monitoring specializations and specialists' remuneration a way to control volumes and prices. Revaluing primary care, on the other hand, would not necessarily make this sector more attractive to medical graduates. For readers who want to explore the insurance framework, the website provides guida LAMal. ## What this means in practice for those looking at Ticino For a cross-border commuter, the most concrete geographic reference in the source is the Canton of Ticino. The assessment related to the canton says that, from 2029, it is estimated that half of citizens could benefit from premium reductions. The figure describes the scenario for reductions, while 5% remains the national figure for 2027. This distinction changes how the news is read. The 5% concerns the national monthly premium; the estimate for Ticino instead concerns the possible distribution of premium reductions. These are two different levels: the first signals the announced increase, the second shows how broad the affected population could be. For those who work across the border, the two figures should therefore be kept separate. ### Costs, redistribution and timing | Proposal | Main lever | Indicated effect or limitation | |---|---|---| | State fund | Operation without profits or dividends | Potentially lower premiums; administrative costs of about 4% and per-person costs treated as the main growth factor | | Premium based on income | Distribution | Costs would change little, with potentially less awareness of costs; in Ticino, the issue of collection according to tax principles arises | | Prevention | Long-term horizon | It is not a definitive solution for premiums in the coming years; a strategy, objectives and an assessment of costs and benefits are needed | | Control of specialists | Volumes and prices | Control of specializations and remuneration can affect both dimensions | | LAMal catalogue | Effectiveness, appropriateness and cost-effectiveness | According to the UFSP, the checks have enabled savings of approximately 150 million francs per year; Grobet calls for more checks | The table separates five levers that may appear equivalent in the debate, but are not. The state fund concerns organization and the absence of profits and dividends; the income-based premium concerns the distribution of financing. Prevention works over the long term, while control of specializations and remuneration targets the volumes and prices of services. Verification of the LAMal catalogue, on the other hand, addresses the effectiveness, appropriateness and cost-effectiveness of the services included. For those who work across the border and follow the cost of living in Ticino, the figure to monitor is therefore not a single percentage. It is necessary to distinguish the announced increase, any reduction in premiums and the effect of the reforms. The confronto del costo della vita can complement this reasoning, without replacing the reading of the assessments reported. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to use expert assessments The news can be turned into a structured verification, without assigning the proposals any additional amounts or rules. For a cross-border worker following the issue in Canton Ticino, it is useful to separate the national figure, the possible reduction in premiums and structural reforms. ### A five-step method 1. Fix the national figure. Write 2027 and a 5% increase in your worksheet. Use it as an editorial starting point, not as an individual calculation: the news concerns the national monthly premium. 2. Classify the proposal. Put the state-run insurer in the management column; the income-based premium in the distribution column; prevention, specialists and the LAMal catalogue in the columns dedicated to system reforms. This separation prevents you from confusing a different distribution of costs with a reduction in them. 3. Verify which problem is being addressed. For the state-run insurer, set Christina Vetsch-Tzogiou's assessment alongside the claim that there are no profits and dividends: under LAMal, profits are not permitted and administrative costs account for approximately 4% of premiums. For the income-linked premium, record instead the assessment that costs would change little and would be distributed differently. 4. Put the proposals in chronological order. The increase figure concerns 2027; the estimate of reductions in Ticino starts in 2029; prevention is described as a long-term contribution and not as a definitive solution for premiums in the coming years. The catalogue reviews, on the other hand, have an estimated saving of about 150 million francs per year. 5. Conclude with the experts' criteria. For LAMal benefits, consider effectiveness, appropriateness and cost-effectiveness; for prevention, look at clear objectives and the relationship between costs and benefits; for specialists, observe the control of volumes and prices. A cross-border worker can thus read the Ticino figure without turning the estimate concerning half of the citizens into an individual amount. The final worksheet should keep three levels distinct: the announced fact, the expert's assessment and the possible consequence. This is a way to remain faithful to the source and not attribute an additional procedure to the reduction in premiums. To complete the check of your budget, open the calcolatore fiscale. *Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/info/dialogo/Casse-malati-i-cittadini-propongono-gli-esperti-rispondono--4135604.html)*

item.title: Tre Valli Varesine 2026: times, route and closures
item.description: October 6: start from Busto Arsizio, finish on Via Sacco at Varese. Six city laps for men and women.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - On Tuesday, October 6th, both Binda races will take place - Women's race starts at 9:15 AM from Busto: finish expected between 12:25 PM and 1:00 PM - Men's race starts at 1:00 PM: finish expected between 5:20 PM and 6:00 PM - Six city laps for both races ## Key facts - Event → 6th Tre Valli Women's Race and 105th Tre Valli Varesine - Start → Busto Arsizio - Finish → Varese, via Sacco - Women's race → start 9:15 AM, finish between 12:25 PM and 1:00 PM - Men's race → start 1:00 PM, finish between 5:20 PM and 6:00 PM - City circuit → six repetitions - Men's long lap → two loops up to Gavirate ### The day's schedule On Tuesday, October 6th, Busto Arsizio and Varese will be the two focal points of the 105th Tre Valli Varesine, preceded on the same day by the 6th Tre Valli Women's Race. Both Binda races start from Busto Arsizio and finish in via Sacco, in Varese. The program begins in the morning with the women's race. The women start at 9:15 AM from via Volta, with the finish expected between 12:25 PM and 1:00 PM. Following the women's race, at lunchtime, it is the turn of the men's classic: the men start at 1:00 PM and are expected to finish between 5:20 PM and 6:00 PM. The temporal distinction is therefore clear. The first race occupies the morning slot, while the second begins at 1:00 PM and continues until the expected conclusion in the late afternoon. The day thus brings together two competitions with the same general starting point and the same finish, but with separate start times and finish times. ### Closures during the passage The sporting calendar is accompanied by a series of road closures along the route. The source notes that roads reopen after the last passage of the cyclists in the affected section. Reopening is therefore linked to the actual transit of the race at that point, after the group has completed the scheduled passage. The end of the transit is indicated by the 'End of race' signal, displayed on some vehicles closing the group. This is the reference point for recognizing when the cyclists' passage in the affected section ends and when the road closure can be lifted. This signaling accompanies the traffic management planned for the two Binda races. Thus, October 6th is described as a day with two distinct moments: first the women's Tre Valli, then the 105th men's Tre Valli Varesine. For both, the general start is set in Busto Arsizio and the finish is expected in Varese, via Sacco, while the transit along the course determines the closures and subsequent reopening of the roads. ## The route between Busto and Varese ### The shared route The two races share a long part of the route. After the start from Busto Arsizio, the group crosses a substantial part of the city and heads toward Solbiate and Fagnano Olona. The route then continues through Cairate, Castelseprio, Carnago, Caronno Varesino, Morazzone, Gazzada Schianno and Buguggiate. From Buguggiate, the race reaches Varese via the SP1, the provincial road along the lake. The route then includes the climb of the Ronchi and the passage through Casbeno, before the first finish on via Sacco. This passage marks the entry into the city circuit that both races must tackle in the shared part of the race. The loop in Varese includes piazza Montegrappa and via Veratti. The group then rides the first section of viale Aguggiari, passes through Montello and continues along via Marzorati-Brunella. The route continues on via Sanvito, via Campigli, via Trentini and via Daverio, then turns onto via Macchi to reach the Schiranna roundabout. From the roundabout, the route enters via Corridoni, on the climb of the Ronchi. The race then returns to via Daverio, crosses piazza Liberta and via XXV Aprile, before rejoining via Sacco. The sequence of roads defines the city circuit designated for the women's Tre Valli and the men's classic. ### The six city laps The city circuit is repeated six times by both the women and the men. The repetition includes the entire loop with piazza Montegrappa, via Veratti, the first section of viale Aguggiari, Montello, via Marzorati-Brunella, via Sanvito, via Campigli, via Trentini, via Daverio, via Macchi, the Schiranna roundabout, via Corridoni, piazza Liberta, via XXV Aprile and via Sacco. After the six laps on the city streets, the men's race adds a different part of the route. The men must in fact tackle the long circuit, extending as far as Gavirate, twice. The split from the city circuit occurs after the Montello climb, when the group descends from Casbeno-Bobbiate toward the lake. ### The men's long lap From the lake, the riders follow the SP1 to Oltrona di Gavirate. Here they tackle the Cinque Piante climb up to Barasso. The return toward Varese passes through Luvinate and Casciago, with a new return to the lake and the repeat of the Ronchi climb. The men ride this long lap twice. The men's race therefore combines the six laps of the city loop with the two additional laps that unfold between the lake, Oltrona di Gavirate, Barasso, Luvinate and Casciago, before returning to the Ronchi section. ### The participants in the men's race The presentation last Tuesday at Ville Ponti enabled Binda to unveil much of the field for the 105a Tre Valli Varesine. The list stayed fairly similar until today, when the organizers released the official start list in the evening. The men's list is headed by McNulty, listed as the world champion. At the last moment, however, Evenepoel withdrew. Many champions nevertheless remain among the entrants, as the presentation dedicated to the race points out. The transition from the presentation to the official list is the follow-up announced by Binda to define the starting field. The lineup made public in the evening maintains the picture already previewed at Ville Ponti, with the change being Evenepoel's absence and McNulty's presence at the top of the list. The list of participants for the women's Tre Valli Women's Race was also made official. The women's race is therefore accompanied by an official list distinct from that of the 105a men's race, following the presentation of the competition and its entrants. The remainder of the day will be covered live by VareseNews. The editorial team will use the same liveblog that hosted, action after action, the 107a Coppa Bernocchi. The race ended in Legnano with Frenchman Noa Isidore's victory. The live coverage will follow Binda's two races as they unfold. The liveblog is thus identified as the space chosen to accompany the cycling day, from the women's race to the men's classic, with coverage of the competition's developments. The announced coverage adds to the information already made public about the starting lists. On the one hand are the official lists, with McNulty leading the men's field and Evenepoel's withdrawal; on the other is the live coverage of the races, entrusted to the same space that covered the Coppa Bernocchi won in Legnano by Noa Isidore. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/guida-alla-tre-valli-varesine-percorsi-chiusure-e-corridori-al-via/2698591/)*

item.title: Bellinzona: merger and 2026 budget compared
item.description: 2025 spending of 235,8 million and 2026 budget of 253,5 million: a look at the costs of the merger.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In 2017 thirteen municipalities became a single City - The promise was greater efficiency and fewer duplications - In 2025, expenditure amounted to 235,8 million and the deficit to 2,7 - In 2026, the budget provides for 253,5 million in expenditure ## Key facts - Merger → 2017: 13 municipalities into a single City - Initial increase in salaries → approximately 3,37 million, equal to 4,7% - 2025 expenditure → 235,8 million francs - 2025 net investments → 25,4 million francs - 2026 budget → 253,5 million in expenditure, deficit of 9,17 million In 2017, Bellinzona changed its face: thirteen municipalities became a single City. Almost ten years later, Elio Del Biaggio proposes stopping the discussion of intentions and measuring the results. The promise was clear: greater efficiency, rationalization, better services, greater investment capacity, and an administrative structure suited to a larger territory. The question concerns not only projects or population growth, but also costs, taxation, services, efficiency, maintenance, and economic development. ### The rationalization challenge The main organizational argument was duplication. Thirteen administrations could have partly duplicate and unnecessary structures and functions. The single City was supposed to consolidate responsibilities, eliminate overlaps, and make better use of staff, streamlining it where necessary. The analysis, however, describes a different outcome: the old structures would have been combined without any real reduction. The result is therefore a larger municipality, but not necessarily a more efficient and less costly one. Already in the initial phase, a comparison of the budgets showed an increase in total salaries of approximately 3,37 million francs, equal to 4,7%. It was the start-up phase, and the figure alone perhaps did not demonstrate a genuine failure. But the requested assessment remains concrete: how much did the merger actually cost, and what structural savings did it produce? The issue also concerns the relationship between staff and services. A modern administration needs competent and motivated people, but the problem arises when new positions and responsibilities do not lead to a proportionate improvement in services. In 2025, the City recorded 235,8 million francs in expenditure, closing with a deficit of 2,7 million, and made 25,4 million in net investments. For 2026, the budget rises to 253,5 million in expenditure, with an expected deficit of 9,17 million. ### From project to service The question of the success of the aggregation cannot be resolved by looking only at the City’s new size. The useful comparison is between what should have changed and what the citizen encounters every day: a neighborhood, a street, a sidewalk, a service, a response from the administration or a tax to pay. Before 2017, the critical point identified by the analysis was the thirteen administrations and their possible overlaps. After unification, the assessment instead concerns the ability to truly reduce structures, duplications and costs. If the old organizations are simply placed side by side within a larger Municipality, the aggregation may change the form without automatically producing greater efficiency. | Area | Promise of the aggregation | Verification indicated by the source | |---|---|---| | Structures | Consolidate responsibilities and eliminate overlaps | How many functions have been consolidated? | | Staff | Make better use of staffing levels and rationalize them | How many positions have been eliminated or created? | | Services | Offer a proportionate improvement | How are services, roads, sidewalks and responses changing? | | Costs | Reduce structures, duplications and expenses | How much does the municipal apparatus cost today compared with the past? | This framework shifts the judgment from the organizational chart to concrete experience. An increase in salaries is not enough, on its own, to demonstrate a failure; likewise, a new responsibility does not by itself demonstrate an improvement. The figure to look for is the relationship between resources employed and services actually perceived. In the available text, the scope remains clearly defined even for the cross-border commuter reader: G permits, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation are not examined. The verifiable object is the City’s machinery, with its expenses, taxation, maintenance and services. To keep the public account separate from the personal budget, one can consult the costo della vita. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ### A five-step reading procedure The source already offers a useful sequence for checking whether the aggregation has kept its promises, without adding assumptions unrelated to the available figures. 1. Establish the basis for comparison: in 2017, thirteen municipalities became a single City. This is the starting point for assessing organizational change. 2. Isolate the start-up phase: the comparison of the budgets indicated an increase in total salaries of approximately 3.37 million francs, equal to 4.7%. 3. Read the 2025 result: 235.8 million francs in expenses, a deficit of 2.7 million and 25.4 million in net investments. 4. Focus on 2026: the budget rises to 253.5 million in expenses and forecasts a deficit of 9.17 million. 5. Check the structure: the final check concerns positions eliminated and created, merged functions, the cost of the municipal administration and the relationship between new responsibilities and services. The fifth step is the one that connects the figures to everyday life. Indeed, the source invites readers to look beyond the organizational chart: citizens live in a neighborhood, travel on roads and sidewalks, use services, wait for responses and pay taxes. Higher costs, bureaucracy or postponed maintenance therefore make precise questions necessary, not generic assessments. To keep the value expressed in francs distinct from the currency comparison, comparatore CHF/EUR is available. The reading of the City's accounts nevertheless remains separate from the individual calculation of salaries. To move from the general figures to your own budget, use calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/rubriche/ospite/1954889/servizi-costi-aggregazione-citta-domanda-bellinzona-successo-elio-biaggio)*

## TL;DR - Lereti works began on Monday, October 5, on via Copelli - Replacement of 400 meters of piping planned - Alternating one-way traffic controlled by a traffic-light system - Indicative completion: November 27, barring unforeseen circumstances ## Key facts - Work: renewal of the water supply network - Section: from the roundabout with via Gorizia to km 17+117 of SP23 - Pipelines: 200 meters of supply and 200 meters of distribution - Connection: one user connection to the new pipes - Restoration: road surfacing at the end of the work ### The project's third lot Lereti's construction site for the renewal of the water supply network began on the morning of Monday, October 5, on via Copelli, in Luino. The project is part of the company's investment plan in Varesotto, designed to increase the efficiency of the water service, reduce leakage, and improve infrastructure monitoring through digitalization. The work is not an isolated intervention. It is the third lot of an overall project launched last year with the pipelines on via Gorizia. At that construction site, one kilometer of new network was laid and, in September, the final resurfacing of the asphalt was completed. For those passing through, this means that the period indicated provides an idea of the expected duration, but does not justify inferring a precise reopening day without further communications. The example of via Gorizia helps clarify the sequence of the project: after one kilometre of new network was laid, the final restoration of the asphalt was completed in September. item.title: Lariana: 8,4 million for safety and road infrastructure
item.description: The Province of Como invests in safety and road accessibility along the S.P. 583 Lariana: new sidewalks, motorcyclist protection barriers and road resurfacing.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Meeting at Villa Gallia on the S.P. 583 Lariana - Provincial program launched in 2018 - Night work on various sections starting October 12 - 8,4 million for additional works ## Key facts - Location → Villa Gallia - Road → S.P. 583 Lariana - Section → from km 1,870 to km 31,300 - Program launch → 2018 - Future investments → 8,4 million euros ### Update on the Lariana A meeting organized by the Province of Como was held today at Villa Gallia to review the work along the S.P. 583 Lariana. The meeting was attended by the Prefect of Como, Corrado Conforto Galli, and the mayors of the municipalities involved in the provincial program. Those present were Angelo Barindelli, Mayor of Bellagio, Alberto Trabucchi, Mayor of Blevio, Angela Molinari, Mayor of Faggeto Lario, Massimo Morini, Mayor of Nesso, Federico Cola, Mayor of Pognana Lario, Rino Malacrida, Mayor of Torno, and Matteo Vanetti, Mayor of Zelbio. Amedeo Gelpi, a councillor, attended on behalf of the Municipality of Lezzeno. Since 2018, the Province of Como has been carrying out a comprehensive program along the section of the Lariana between km 1,870, in Como, and km 31,300, in Bellagio. The stated objective is to improve the road’s safety and usability for all users, with particular attention to pedestrians and vulnerable users. The program concerns more than just the roadway. A significant part of the work has been devoted to securing the slopes above the road, also through PNRR resources allocated to tackling hydrogeological instability. The works have involved the areas of Como, Torno, Blevio, Faggeto Lario, Pognana Lario, Nesso, Lezzeno and Bellagio. ### Completed works, construction sites and projects During the meeting, an overall picture was presented of the works already completed, those under way and the planned interventions. The discussion thus brought together in a single update the various types of work planned along the provincial road: slope safety, pedestrian paths, bridges, tunnels, barriers and renewal of road surfaces. The meeting also made it possible to gather from the mayors needs, ideas and proposals concerning further work on the Lariana and the connected road network. The Province stated that its goal is to define future priorities together with the local areas and direct the available resources accordingly. The update discussed at Villa Gallia therefore concerns both the status of works already included in the program and the planning of the next activities on the provincial road network. ### Municipality-by-Municipality Works The overview presented by the Province includes works of different characteristics and dimensions in the municipalities along the Lariana. In Bellagio, work on new raised sidewalks in San Giovanni, covering approximately 224 meters, was handed over on September 3, with an investment of 600 mila euro. The pedestrian paths at Vergonese and ex Cementeria, covering approximately 500 meters, were also completed in 2021 in the municipal area. In Visgnola, securing the valley-side edge and new sidewalks have been planned, with an investment of 200 mila euro. In Blevio, the program includes the new bridge over the Covercin stream, for 150 mila euro, and repairs to the Pertus and Girola bridges. These two structures were damaged in September 2025, and the repair work is worth 630 mila euro. Also in Blevio, the systems in the Blevio I, II and III tunnels are to be upgraded, for 800 mila euro. In Torno, by contrast, upgrading the tunnel systems involves an investment of 600 mila euro. At Faggeto Lario, new standards-compliant barriers equipped with motorcyclist-protection devices are planned, covering approximately 1.000 meters and with an investment of 700 mila euro. At Pognana Lario, the project concerns widening the Quarzano bridge, with an investment of 1 milione di euro. At Lezzeno, new raised sidewalks are planned in the direction of the Ponte del Diavolo, covering approximately 530 meters, as well as the consolidation of two bridges, with a total investment of 1,5 milioni di euro. Particular attention has also been paid to S.P. 44, which is connected to the Lariana, in the territories of Veleso and Zelbio. At Veleso, new reinforced-concrete shoulders and guardrails are planned, funded by the Province for 400 mila euro. At Zelbio, resurfacing and slope-load-reduction works are planned along the Nesso-Veleso-Zelbio stretch. A program agreement is also indicated for regularizing the registration of the municipal roads along S.P. 44. The President of the Province, Fiorenzo Bongiasca, summarized the authority’s position: > «The safety and passability of our road network remain one of the Province’s priorities – President Fiorenzo Bongiasca emphasizes – On the Lariana, we are carrying out an important program of works, and we know there is still much to do.» The statement recalls the twofold objective set out in the program: to address road safety and improve its usability through works compatible with the characteristics of the individual areas. ### The schedule for the upcoming construction sites Starting October 12, work to renew the road surfaces on various sections of the Lariana will begin at night to limit disruption to traffic. The schedule covers five areas of the provincial road: - in Blevio, approximately 700 meters in the built-up area; - in Torno, approximately 600 meters in the built-up area; - in Faggeto Lario, approximately 700 meters at the intersection with the S.P. 43; - between Pognana Lario and Nesso, approximately 800 meters from Quarzano to Careno; - in Lezzeno, approximately 400 meters in specific sections of the built-up area. In addition to this work, further interventions funded with ministerial funds are already planned for the 2027-2028 and 2030-2031 periods. The overall investment indicated by the Province is 8,4 million euros. The funding was also obtained thanks to the involvement of former senator Armando Valli, who followed and supported the process for allocating the resources. The program linked to the new funds provides for the replacement and upgrading of road restraint systems. It also includes bringing the road’s geometric characteristics and its intersections into compliance with current regulations. Where the terrain allows, turning spaces may be created, with the aim of improving the road’s safety and functionality. The Province also plans raised walkways outside the carriageway in sections where the characteristics of the road and terrain allow. These works will complete the pedestrian routes already built in recent years. ### The agreement being finalized with Blevio During the meeting, architect Fedele Mora, head of the Infrastructure Department of the Province of Como, also presented the proposals for a program agreement currently being finalized between the Province and the Municipality of Blevio. The project concerns further works at four strategic points in the area and is divided into four operational lots. The proposals include work at Pertus, in the immediate vicinity of the school. The lot includes demolition of the existing building along the S.P. 583, widening of the provincial roadway and redevelopment of the torrential drainage channel. The agreement and resource planning are the next steps identified by the Province to continue work on the Lariana and the connected road network. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/lago-di-como-maxi-investimenti-anti-ingorgo-e-barriere-salva-motociclisti-rivoluzione-viabilita-sulla-lariana/)*

The news places a precise question at the center: how much remains in your pocket when you work more, but a higher salary comes with lower benefits? The substance of the approval is stated clearly: approval for a detailed analysis and simulations of the impact of the relationship between higher salary and fewer benefits. However, the text does not provide a figure, percentage, or already-calculated result. Nor does it indicate an implementation date or a formula for measuring the individual balance. ### What was decided The verifiable fact therefore concerns the step described by the source. Avanti's motion passes, and the Grand Council supports Speziali's report (Plr). The matter is not presented as a new amount already granted to workers, but as an analysis accompanied by simulations. The news item does not report additional statements, nor does it identify a sector, professional category, or income bracket involved. For those who are cross-border workers and work in Ticino, the issue can be read as an examination of the relationship between higher salary and fewer benefits. However, the source does not say that this step already changes the payslip or the conditions of a particular category. The text contains no references to G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax refunds, withholding tax, new 2026 tax agreement, or double taxation. This distinction defines the scope of the news item. The reader can note the approval, the name of the report, the motion's political origin, and the type of work requested. However, they cannot derive from the text a personal amount, a specific benefit, or a deadline. The headline raises a question about working more; the material provided goes no further than approval for the analysis and simulations. To read this passage from the cross-border worker's perspective, the first distinction is between decision and outcome. The decision has been made: the Grand Council has given the green light to Speziali (Plr)'s report and to the approach calling for a detailed analysis with simulations. The economic outcome, however, is not contained in the source. We therefore do not know which salary is used, which benefits are compared, or what balance the calculation produces. ### The comparison permitted by the source | Item | Available data | |---|---| | Decision | Green light from the Grand Council | | Report | Speziali (Plr) | | Instrument | Detailed analysis and simulations | | Outcome | Not reported in the text provided | For a cross-border worker, this separation avoids a practical error: treating the announcement of an analysis as if it were already a new salary rule. Keep the two elements of the comparison distinct: higher salary and fewer benefits. 4. Verify the presence of figures and criteria before turning the comparison into a personal estimate. item.description: The Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo in Collina d 'Oro invests 12 million francs, closes for months and announces 76 redundancies out of 81 employees.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo to close for several months - Planned investment: 12 million francs - 76 layoffs out of 81 employees - Construction completion expected: May 1 ## Key facts - Property → Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo - Location → Collina d'Oro - Owner → Dot Life SA - Investment → 12 million francs - Current workforce → 81 employees - Announced layoffs → 76 employees - Formal notification → October-November 2026 - Last actual working day → December 30 Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo in Collina d'Oro, in the Canton of Ticino, is preparing to close its doors for several months. The owner company Dot Life SA has planned a modernization project costing 12 million francs, with the aim of bringing the property up to modern standards. The investment, however, is accompanied by a major downsizing: the announced layoffs concern 76 of the 81 employees currently working there. The temporary closure had already been foreshadowed by rumors in mid-September. The owner's decisions define both the pause in the work and the management of the staff. The workforce figure refers to the employees currently working at the property. The closure, on the other hand, is described as temporary and linked to the modernization project: the plan does not announce the end of the hotel, but rather a suspension lasting several months. The outlook indicated by the company remains selective, because it concerns the employees who will be needed when operations resume. ### The staff schedule The most significant impact concerns the cuts. Formal notification of the layoffs is expected between October and November 2026. Only a few department heads will be temporarily spared, while the overwhelming majority of workers will reach their last actual working day on December 30. December 31, on the other hand, will be a paid leave day. Dot Life's letter also provides for some support measures and a “loyalty bonus” for those who remain present at work until the last day established by the contract. The measure is therefore linked to continued attendance until the contractual expiry date indicated by the company. ### The plan after the work The next phase remains open. Dot Life emphasizes the temporary nature of the measure and expresses its intention to rehire the employees who will be needed when operations resume. Construction is expected to be completed by May 1, but the company has acknowledged that it cannot currently guarantee the rehiring of all current employees. This is the main point of uncertainty for those currently working at the hotel: the investment has a defined horizon, but the return of the staff does not. What changes for a cross-border worker For a cross-border worker who works in the structure, the dossier allows reconstructing the dates but not attributing an individual outcome. The figure of 76 layoffs concerns the group of currently employed staff; the source does not indicate how many are cross-border workers nor does it clarify whether each position will follow exactly the same schedule. The first caution, therefore, is not to transform the total number into a count of border workers involved. ### Four steps to separate The picture becomes more readable by separating what the letter makes concrete from what remains conditional: | Step | Reported data | What cannot be deduced | |---|---|---| | Communication | October‑November 2026 | it is not the actual exit date | | Last day | 30 December for the vast majority | it is not indicated as an identical calendar for everyone | | Leave | 31 December, paid | it follows the actual last working day | | Sites | expected end 1 May | it does not equate to guaranteed re‑hiring | For those working across the border, the text does not go into the details of G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, INPS, withholding tax or double taxation. It does not indicate procedures, forms or effects on these institutions. Therefore one cannot deduce from the hotel’s closure an automatic change of administrative or fiscal status: these are elements external to the reported information. The useful comparison is between two scenarios. In the first, the relationship reaches the date indicated for the majority and 31 December follows with paid leave; the loyalty bonus is linked to presence up to the last contractual day. In the second, the sites end on 1 May and Dot Life evaluates re‑hiring the necessary staff, without guarantee for all. The difference between intention and guarantee is the practical point not to be confused. Regarding solely the job title, whoever needs to check the general rules can consult the guide on the 'Permesso G/B' Permesso G/B, without attributing to Dot Life indications that the source does not provide. For a payroll estimate, the 'calcolatore fiscale' calcolatore fiscale requires personal data that the article does not contain. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## From the communication to the next steps Practical handling can remain anchored to the documents and dates already announced. There is no need to fill the gaps with a reopening date or a guarantee of returning that the company has not made. ### Checklist based on the letter 1. Keep the formal notice of the layoffs, scheduled between October and November 2026, and read the accompanying measures that Dot Life has announced. 2. Check the personal schedule indicated by the company. December 30 is the effective last day for the vast majority; December 31 is indicated as paid leave. 3. Check the condition linked to the loyalty bonus: the letter grants it to those who will ensure their presence until the last day established by the contract. It should not be confused with an amount or condition different from what is written. 4. Keep construction work and rehiring separate. May 1 is the scheduled date for the end of the construction work; Dot Life talks about rehiring the necessary employees, but admits it cannot guarantee all current employees. For a cross-border worker, this sequence avoids treating the rumors from mid-September as a formal communication and considering May 1 an automatic return. The source does not provide forms, contacts or deadlines for a possible period of unemployment; it is therefore not possible to attribute a specific procedure to an entity or a benefit. To orient oneself regarding the next step, one can use the tool on disoccupazione frontalieri, keeping verification of the individual case separate. The same criterion applies to income: the article contains the investment amount and the number of employees involved, but not individual salary data. Estimating net income requires personal information and cannot be derived from 12 million francs. To estimate the effect on income using your own data, use calcolatore fiscale. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/canton-ticino-lhotel-di-lusso-chiude-per-rifarsi-il-look-con-12-milioni-e-licenzia-76-dipendenti/)*

## In breve - 12 million francs for the modernization - 76 layoffs out of 81 employees - For the majority, last day December 30 - Construction works expected to finish May 1 ## Fatti chiave - Structure → Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo - Location → Collina d'Oro - Owner → Dot Life SA - Investment → 12 million francs - Staff involved → 76 employees out of 81 - Formal communication → October-November 2026 - Paid leave → December 31 - Expected end of works → May 1 A 12 million franc investment will accompany the Hotel Villa Principe Leopoldo in Collina d'Oro towards a deep modernization project. To start the works, the structure is preparing to close its doors for several months. The plan is from the owning company Dot Life SA and the temporary closure had already been rumoured in mid-September. The operation, designed to bring the hotel up to modern standards, will however have a very heavy occupational cost. The announced layoffs concern 76 of the 81 currently employed staff. Only a few department heads will remain, at least temporarily. The formal communication of the cuts is expected between October and November 2026. For the vast majority of staff, the calendar indicated in the company letter sets December 30 as the actual last working day behind the scenes. December 31 will follow a paid leave day. The same communication also provides for some accompanying measures and a loyalty bonus for those who guarantee their presence at work until the last day set by the contract. ### The project and the uncertainty of return Dot Life defines the measure as temporary and expresses the intention to rehire the collaborators that will be needed when activity resumes. However, the plan does not amount to a general confirmation of jobs. The expected date for the end of works is May 1, while the company has admitted it is currently unable to guarantee the rehiring of all current employees. The calendar thus lines up an autumn communication, the conclusion of work at the end of December, and a possible return after the works. The source distinguishes these steps and does not present rehiring as automatic. For the hotel employees, the central datum remains the distance between the announced investment and the announced reduction of staff: 12 million destined for the structure, 76 positions involved in the plan. The project therefore concerns both the refurbishment of the hotel and the management of an occupational phase already marked by precise dates. ## For the cross-border worker, certainty concerns the job For those who work in Canton Ticino and cross the border, the news has a concrete point: an employer is announcing a temporary closure and a significant staff reduction. However, the source does not clarify whether there are cross-border workers among the hotel's 81 employees. Therefore, it is not possible to turn Dot Life's plan into an automatic consequence for the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, double taxation, rebates or INPS. The text documents a company plan; it does not describe tax or social security changes. The practical reading lies in the difference between intention and guarantee. Dot Life says it intends to rehire the employees needed for the resumption, but admits that it cannot guarantee everyone will return. The decisive word is therefore needed: the number of positions that will become available again is not indicated, and there is no general confirmation for those currently working at the facility. Nor is the temporary retention of a few department heads accompanied by criteria or a more precise duration. ### Three possible positions in the plan | Situation indicated | What the source allows one to say | |---|---| | Staff included among the 76 | The reduction will be formally communicated between October and November 2026; for the majority, the actual last day will be December 30. | | A few department heads | Their retention is described as temporary. | | Employees needed for the resumption | Dot Life expresses the intention to rehire them, without guaranteeing all current employees. | For a cross-border worker, this distinction avoids an excessive interpretation: the source does not say that the G permit will change, that AVS or LPP will be suspended, that LAMal will be modified, or that withholding tax will result in different treatment. Nor does it provide information on double taxation, rebates or dealings with INPS. The only documented scenario is employment-related and remains tied to the company letter, the dates indicated and the possibility—by no means certain—of future re-employment. Anyone who needs to consider alternatives can consult annunci di lavoro, without presenting a return to the hotel as already secured. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Operational steps for those involved The text of the corporate communication is the operational reference to follow the announced schedule. The source puts on the table dates, accompanying measures, loyalty bonus and a possible return. The path can therefore remain anchored to these elements, without adding unwritten conditions. ### The sequence to follow 1. Between October and November 2026, verify the formal communication of the cuts. It is the window indicated to make the announcements on personnel effective. In this phase the point to clarify is your placement in the plan: among the 76 employees concerned or among the few department heads destined to remain temporarily. 2. Read Dot Life's letter in the section dedicated to accompanying measures. The communication also provides a loyalty bonus for those who will guarantee their work presence until the last day set by the contract. The datum to keep fixed is the link between the recognition and presence until the contractual expiry. 3. Mark two separate dates. December 30 is the actual last day behind the scenes for the vast majority; December 31 is indicated as a paid leave day. They must not be fused into a single deadline, because the letter presents them distinctly. 4. Treat May 1 as the expected date for the end of the works, not as a promise of return for all. Dot Life talks about rehiring the collaborators necessary for the resumption, but does not guarantee all current employees. For those seeking continuity it may be useful to alongside reading the letter the job announcements and the information on cross-border unemployment. For a cross-border worker, control remains limited to the employment relationship described by the source: no change of G permit, withholding tax or other fiscal and social security institutions is documented. item.description: Saturday, October 17, in the warehouse next to the Gottardo Arena, bingo, a screened match and a party: every franc raised will be invested in Hcap shares.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Saturday, October 17 public event next to the Gottardo Arena - Every franc collected will go into Hcap shares - Raffle from 3 p.m. and match at 7:45 p.m. - Party with music until 2 a.m. ## Key facts - When → Saturday, October 17 - Where → tent in front of the Gottardo Arena - Objective → purchase Hcap shares - Maccheronata → 5 francs per portion - Celebratory scarf → 10 francs ### A collection with a precise destination On Saturday, October 17, Ambrì-Piotta fans will be at the centre of a public event in the tent in front of the Gottardo Arena. The initiative has been designed to raise the funds needed to finance the purchase of Hcap shares and to make supporters protagonists of the future of the Hockey Club Ambrì Piotta. The economic point of the proposal is defined in the announcement: the entire amount collected will be converted into company shares. The destination of the collection is therefore linked to the purchase of Hcap shares, according to a formula presented as ambitious and concrete. The project is accompanied by the hope that the initiative can provide the club with solid and community foundations to invest in the future. The day in the tent represents the public moment indicated to support this objective and to bring the white‑and‑blue world together around the club. The reference to every franc collected defines the destination of the mobilisation. The text indeed links the collection to the transformation of money into shares and to the possibility for fans to participate in Hcap’s future as shareholders. The source places the appointment in the tent in front of the Gottardo Arena. This is the space indicated for the public event, while the programme continues from the afternoon, through the match, to the evening party. The open nature of the initiative and its share‑holding purpose are therefore the two elements declared in the news. On one hand there is the public meeting on October 17; on the other, the fundraising needed to buy shares in the club. The message addressed to supporters is to become protagonists of Ambrì‑Piotta’s future. ## The project comes from the biancoblù community ### The press release and the organizers The press release outlining the reasons for the mobilization is signed by Luca Dattrino, a journalist, writer and teacher who has already authored books dedicated to the Leventine club. His signature accompanies the presentation of the initiative and its objective, defined as ambitious and concrete. In the text, the mobilization is described as having sprung from the very heart of the biancoblù community. The hope expressed is that the club can receive solid, community-based foundations on which to invest in the future. These are the words used to explain the value attributed to the initiative. The press release also defines the collective nature of the participation. It does so by naming the groups and people who care about the team: > The grassroots initiative brings together everyone who cares about Ambrì-Piotta: Gioventù biancoblù, Gruppo di sostegno, Interclub, Donatoren, Curva Sud, fans and enthusiasts. The same sentence places Gioventù biancoblù, Gruppo di sostegno, Interclub, Donatoren and Curva Sud alongside fans and enthusiasts. In the press release, these names make up the base from which the mobilization arises and indicate the scope of participation around Ambrì-Piotta. The reference to grassroots origins therefore accompanies the list of groups involved. The source presents the initiative as a meeting point between organized groups and individual supporters, all united by their attention to the biancoblù colors. The community dimension is not separate from the stated objective: to provide the club with solid foundations on which to invest in the future. Luca Dattrino’s role is to set out the reasons for the mobilization through the press release. His experience as a journalist, writer and teacher, together with the books dedicated to the Leventine club, supports the explanation of the initiative. The text thus gives a public form to a fundraiser presented as having sprung from the grassroots and supported by the entire biancoblù community. ## The event program ### From bingo to the party The program spreads the activities across the afternoon, evening and night. The day begins with a super bingo and continues with the aperitif, dinner, the match and the closing party. | Moment | Program | |---|---| | From 15 | Super bingo with great prizes | | 17.30 | Social aperitif | | Dinner | Macaroni dish at 5 francs per serving | | 19.45 | Match against Ginevra Servette | | After the match | Party until 2 | The match against Ginevra Servette will start at 19.45 and will also be screened on a giant screen inside the warehouse. After the match, the evening will continue until 2 with music from the 70s, 80s and 90s, a refreshment stand and food offerings. The program also includes appearances by the first-team players. The former greats who once honored the blue-and-white colors will already be there from early afternoon, thus joining the event activities even before the start of the match. Throughout the day, commemorative scarves will be on sale for 10 francs. The sale is listed among the event’s activities, alongside bingo, the aperitif, dinner and the musical evening. On the lawn in front of the rink, visitors will be able to admire Ghiaccio Fuoco, the monumental work by artist Ivan Tresoldi. The composition brings together and interweaves ninety words representing the blue-and-white identity. The presentation describes it as a unique work, worth seeing during the day. item.title: More trips, less you pay: with FAIRTIQ, discounts of up to 20%
item.description: Bonus active from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, with automatic discounts of up to 20% on subsequent trips in Ticino. Monthly thresholds of 10, 50 and 100 francs.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Bonus active from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027 - Maximum discount of 20% on subsequent trips - Monthly thresholds of 10, 50 and 100 francs - Trips that start and end in Ticino qualify ## Key facts - Name → FAIRTIQ Bonus Ticino - Promoters → ABL, AMSA, ARL, FART, FLP, SNL and TPL - Discounts → 5%, 10% and 20% - Check → Rewards > FAIRTIQ Switzerland Bonus - Network → entire cantonal network available through FAIRTIQ - Collaboration → since 2024 From October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027, those who use FAIRTIQ to travel in Ticino can receive automatic discounts of up to 20% on subsequent trips. The initiative is called FAIRTIQ Bonus Ticino and is promoted by seven transport companies: Autolinee Bleniesi (ABL), Autolinea Mendrisiense (AMSA), Autolinee Regionali Luganesi (ARL), Ferrovie Autolinee Regionali Ticinesi (FART), Ferrovie Luganesi (FLP), Società Navigazione del Lago di Lugano (SNL) and Trasporti Pubblici Luganesi (TPL). ### How participation works No specific registration is required. For those who use FAIRTIQ, participation is automatic and free. The app works as usual: you start the trip before boarding and end it once you arrive. The price is calculated automatically, as is any discount provided by the bonus. The threshold is measured against the amount spent through the app over the course of a month. When spending reaches 10 francs, a 5% discount takes effect on subsequent trips. At 50 francs, the discount rises to 10%; at 100 francs, it reaches 20%. The count resets to zero at the beginning of each month. The benefit therefore does not apply to trips already taken: it takes effect after the relevant threshold has been reached. ### Which trips qualify FAIRTIQ trips that start and end within Ticino are included. The initiative covers the entire cantonal network available through the app, not just the routes operated by the seven promoting companies. FFS and AutoPostale lines within the canton are also included. For a cross-border commuter who uses public transport, the point of reference is therefore the network accessible via FAIRTIQ in Canton Ticino. Information on the mezzi pubblici Ticino network helps clarify the initiative's operational scope without mistaking it for merely the list of promoters. The companies have been collaborating with FAIRTIQ since 2024, and the six months of the bonus also provide a period in which to observe the effects of an incentive linked to the actual use of public transport on regional mobility. For a cross-border commuter traveling by public transport, the first practical check concerns the boundary of the individual journey. The bonus does not depend solely on whether the line is operated by one of the seven companies: the source also considers the entire cantonal network available through FAIRTIQ, including FFS and AutoPostale, but requires the journey to begin and end within Ticino. If the FAIRTIQ itinerary begins outside the canton, it does not meet the stated condition; a journey begun and concluded within the cantonal territory, however, follows the applicable criterion. For the cross-border commuter reader, the scope of this news should be kept distinct: the source discusses FAIRTIQ journeys in Canton Ticino and not G permits, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates or withholding tax. ### Variable spending, progressive threshold The model is designed for people who use public transport with varying frequency. There is no need to purchase a pass or incur an upfront expense: the principle described is to pay only for the journeys actually taken, leaving the app to calculate the price automatically. | Spending reached during the month | Discount on subsequent journeys | |---|---| | 10 francs | 5% | | 50 francs | 10% | | 100 francs | 20% | The practical result changes depending on when the threshold is reached. If spending reaches 50 francs, for example, the 10% applies to subsequent journeys, not to those that brought the spending to that level. At the beginning of the following month, the count starts again from zero and the progression must begin anew. Those who travel occasionally may stop before reaching the first threshold; those who use public transport more often may move toward the next level. In both cases, how the app works does not change. Anyone wishing to supplement this reading with a comparison of the cost of a private vehicle can use costo auto pendolare, keeping that calculation separate from the FAIRTIQ mechanism. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. To apply the bonus correctly, the procedure remains FAIRTIQ's standard one. No forms or separate registration are needed: participation is automatic and free for anyone who uses the app. ### The operational sequence 1. Before boarding, open FAIRTIQ and start the journey. 2. Check that the journey you want to count starts within Ticino and is scheduled to end in the canton, a condition required for the bonus. 3. Once you arrive, end the journey in the app. 4. Let FAIRTIQ automatically calculate the price and any applicable discount. 5. Open the Rewards > FAIRTIQ Switzerland Bonus section to check the discount reached and your progress toward the next level. The in-app check also serves to track the spending accumulated during the month. The first threshold is set at 10 francs, the intermediate one at 50 francs and the highest one at 100 francs. After each threshold, the discount applies only to subsequent journeys. For this reason, it is advisable to check the level reached before considering the price of the following trip. The period to remember runs from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027. The monthly tally does not carry over progress from one month to the next: at the beginning of each month, it starts again from zero. The network considered is not limited to the seven promoting companies, but includes the connections available through FAIRTIQ throughout the canton, including the FFS and AutoPostale lines within Ticino. To add a separate calculation tool to expense tracking, consult calcolatore fiscale. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/attualita/1954816/fairtiq-bonus-viaggi-aziende-ticino-sconti)*

item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - TicinoSkills 2026 took place from October 1 to 3 in Gordola - 44 apprentices competed in the regional championships - More than 600 students visited the event - Nearly 400 attendees took part in the day with families ## Key facts - Event → TicinoSkills & Porte Aperte - Dates → from October 1 to 3, 2026 - Venue → SSIC TI Vocational Training Centre, Gordola - Support → Department of Education, Culture and Sport (DECS) - Participants → 44 apprentices - Visitors for career guidance → more than 600 students - Saturday attendance → nearly 400 - Anniversary → 50 years of the SSIC TI Vocational Training Centre ### Three days of competition and career guidance From October 1 to 3, 2026, Gordola hosted the seventh edition of TicinoSkills & Porte Aperte. The event took place at the SSIC TI Vocational Training Centre, with the support of the Department of Education, Culture and Sport (DECS), and combined the regional championships for professions in the building trades with opportunities to explore careers. The edition was a great success. A total of 44 apprentices competed in the regional championships for professions in the building trades. The event combined competition among the contestants with the presence of students, families and visitors interested in learning more about vocational training. During the three days, more than 600 students exploring their career options visited the event. The visit offered the opportunity to discover new professions, find inspiration and gain ideas for the future or a new passion. The students’ participation complemented the competitions with a moment dedicated to those considering their own path. Saturday added a family and community dimension. As part of the Millestrade project, families were at the centre of the day, with nearly 400 attendees recorded on site. At the same time, the entire population was invited to take part in the celebrations marking 50 years of the SSIC TI Vocational Training Centre. It was therefore not an event reserved solely for contestants. The programme involved apprentices competing in the championships, students exploring their career options, families and the general public, with the Gordola Centre serving as the common venue for the various activities. DECS support accompanied an event dedicated to the skills and opportunities offered by vocational training. The programme concluded with the awards ceremony on Saturday, October 3, 2026. On that day, the new Ticino champions were proclaimed, bringing to a close three days dedicated to regional competitions, career guidance and celebrations marking the centre’s fiftieth anniversary. ## The championship results ### The seven regional podiums The awards ceremony on Saturday, October 3, 2026, was a particularly moving moment. The associated companies and locations are indicated alongside the names of the award winners. On the metal construction welders' podium, the three places are occupied by Leonardo Bargiga, Simone Amicucci, and Antonio Iraci, all listed with Ghidoni SA in Riazzino. They highlighted the value of the competition as an opportunity for personal and professional growth, beyond the mere outcome of the rankings. The spirit of the event also involved visitors. Seeing professions up close helps girls and boys concretely discover the possibilities offered by an apprenticeship and imagine their future. The message thus links the experience gained during the event to the choice of career path. The director also recalled DECS's commitment throughout the year through the Millestrade platform. The stated objective is to create opportunities for direct encounters among young people, parents, professions, schools and the world of work. The Gordola event fit into this perspective through visits by students, family participation and interaction with the professions represented in the championships. Thanks for the event's success went to the professional associations, the male and female trainers, as well as the male and female apprentices who contributed to it. It was also extended to all the people involved in the event, which brought competitions, career guidance and public participation to Gordola. *Source: [ticinonews.ch](https://www.ticinonews.ch/ticino/ticinoskills-2026-tre-giorni-di-competizioni-e-scoperte-professionali-a-gordola-443977)*
